source: The Harlow Bay desalination plant began operating in March 2023 after six years of planning and a construction budget of 412 million dollars. Designed by the engineering firm Marlowe and Pryce, the facility uses reverse osmosis to produce 90 million liters of drinking water per day, enough for roughly 600,000 residents. Early critics warned that the plant would harm marine life near the outfall pipe, so the operators installed diffusers that spread the concentrated brine over a wide area. Monitoring by the state environmental agency in 2024 found that salinity returned to normal within 150 meters of the outlet. However, the plant consumes about 3.4 kilowatt-hours of electricity for every cubic meter of water, and the city council is now negotiating a contract for a solar farm to cover 40 percent of that demand by 2027.
target_summary: Harlow Bay's desalination plant has supplied 90 million liters daily since 2023.

source: In 1387 the weavers of Veldmark formed a guild that would dominate the town's economy for nearly two centuries. Membership required a seven-year apprenticeship, a fee of twelve silver marks, and the completion of a master piece judged by three senior weavers. The guild fixed the price of wool cloth, limited each workshop to four looms, and punished members who sold inferior fabric by fining them or confiscating their goods. These rules protected quality and kept wages stable, but they also blocked newcomers and discouraged innovation. When Flemish merchants introduced lighter, cheaper cloth in the 1530s, the guild refused to adapt, and by 1560 more than half of its workshops had closed. Historians now point to Veldmark as a clear example of how rigid regulation can preserve a trade while quietly undermining its future.
target_summary: Veldmark's weavers guild, founded 1387, dominated the town until rigidity caused decline.

source: A 2022 study of 3,200 high school students followed their sleep habits for one academic year. Researchers found that students who slept fewer than seven hours on school nights were 1.8 times more likely to report low mood and scored an average of 9 points lower on standardized math tests than classmates who slept eight hours or more. The team also tested a school that delayed its start time from 7:30 to 8:30 a.m. After the change, average nightly sleep rose by 41 minutes and late arrivals fell by 27 percent. The authors caution that the study cannot prove that sleep alone caused the improvements, since the later start also gave students more time for breakfast. Even so, they recommend that school districts consider later start times for adolescents.
target_summary: Short-sleeping teens had worse mood and math scores; later school starts improved sleep.

source: Tindal Coffee Roasters reported revenue of 18.6 million dollars for fiscal 2024, an increase of 14 percent over the previous year. Most of the growth came from its subscription service, which added 22,000 customers and now accounts for 38 percent of sales. Wholesale revenue to cafes fell 6 percent because two large clients switched to cheaper suppliers. The company opened its fifth retail location in Portland in October and plans two more in 2025, funded by a 3 million dollar credit line. Chief executive Dana Okafor said rising green coffee prices cut gross margin from 46 to 41 percent, and that the firm will raise subscription prices by about 5 percent in January rather than reduce bean quality.
target_summary: Tindal Coffee's 2024 revenue rose 14 percent to 18.6 million dollars.

source: Version 4.2 of the Kestrel router firmware, released on 9 June, fixes a security flaw that allowed attackers on the same network to read stored Wi-Fi passwords. The vulnerability, tracked as KST-2024-117, was discovered by researcher Lena Brandt and reported privately in February. The manufacturer took four months to ship a patch, which drew criticism from security groups that recommend a 90-day disclosure window. The update also adds support for the WPA3 standard, improves guest network isolation, and reduces idle power use by roughly 8 percent. Owners of the older K200 and K300 models will not receive the fix because those devices reached end of support in 2021, and the company advises replacing them. Users can install the update from the router's administration page.
target_summary: Kestrel firmware 4.2 patches a flaw exposing stored Wi-Fi passwords.

source: Farmers in the highland village of Banaoy have maintained stone-walled rice terraces for more than 400 years, sharing a single irrigation network fed by a mountain spring. Each household is assigned a water schedule by a council of elders, and the terraces are planted once a year after a ritual held in November. In recent years, however, younger residents have been leaving for jobs in the lowlands, and nearly a quarter of the terraces now lie fallow. A cooperative formed in 2021 pays volunteers 350 pesos per day to repair walls and clear channels, and it has begun marketing a heritage red rice at 120 pesos per kilogram, double the standard price. Early results are promising: abandoned terraces fell from 24 to 17 percent in two years, and six families have returned to farming.
target_summary: Banaoy's ancient rice terraces are being revived by a cooperative paying volunteers.

source: The Calder County library system launched a program in September that lets children read aloud to trained therapy dogs. Sessions run for 20 minutes on Saturday mornings at four branches, and each child may attend up to twice a month. Librarians say the dogs lower anxiety for hesitant readers, who often fear being corrected by adults or classmates. Of the 310 children who enrolled in the first semester, 64 percent increased their reading level by at least half a grade, according to teacher surveys. The program is run by volunteers from the nonprofit Paws and Pages, and costs the library about 5,200 dollars per year for insurance and training materials. Officials hope to expand to all eleven branches by next fall if donations continue.
target_summary: Calder County libraries let children read aloud to therapy dogs.

source: Mateo Silva won the 2024 Rivermouth Marathon in two hours, eleven minutes and four seconds, finishing 38 seconds ahead of defending champion Joseph Kiprop. Silva, a 27-year-old schoolteacher from Lisbon, ran the first half conservatively and then surged at the 30-kilometer mark, where steady rain and a headwind had slowed the leading pack. It was his first major victory and the fastest time on the course in six years. In the women's race, Hanna Berg of Norway broke the course record with a time of 2:24:50, beating the previous mark by almost two minutes. Race organizers reported 14,800 finishers out of 16,000 registered runners, and raised 1.2 million dollars for local children's hospitals through charity entries.
target_summary: Mateo Silva won the 2024 Rivermouth Marathon in 2:11:04.

source: Between 2015 and 2023, the city of Marquand planted 48,000 street trees as part of a plan to cut summer heat in its densest neighborhoods. Satellite measurements show that blocks with the most new trees are now an average of 2.3 degrees Celsius cooler on summer afternoons than comparable blocks without them. The program focused on low-income areas, which had historically had the least shade and the highest rates of heat-related emergency calls. Nevertheless, about 15 percent of the young trees have died, mainly because of drought and damage from construction. To address this, the city has hired eight arborists, begun a watering program using volunteers, and shifted toward hardier species such as honey locust and hackberry. The next phase aims to add 30,000 trees by 2030.
target_summary: Marquand's 48,000 new street trees cooled dense neighborhoods by 2.3 degrees.

source: Financial planners generally recommend keeping an emergency fund equal to three to six months of essential expenses, but the right amount depends on how stable a person's income is. A salaried government worker with no dependents might be comfortable with three months, while a freelancer or a single-income household with children may need closer to nine. The money should sit in an account that is safe and easy to reach, such as a high-yield savings account, rather than in stocks, whose value can fall just when cash is needed. Many advisers suggest building the fund gradually by automating a transfer of 10 percent of each paycheck. Once the target is reached, the same transfer can be redirected to retirement savings or debt repayment.
target_summary: Emergency funds should cover three to six months of essential expenses.

source: Octopuses have three hearts, blue blood, and a brain that is spread between a central mass and the nerve clusters in their eight arms. Two of the hearts pump blood through the gills, while the third circulates it to the rest of the body and stops beating when the animal swims, which is one reason octopuses prefer to crawl. Their blood uses copper-based hemocyanin instead of iron-based hemoglobin, which carries oxygen efficiently in cold, low-oxygen water. Roughly two thirds of an octopus's neurons are located in its arms, allowing each arm to taste, touch, and react semi-independently. Most species live only one to two years, and females typically die soon after their eggs hatch, having guarded them without feeding for several weeks.
target_summary: Octopuses have three hearts, blue blood, and arm-based neurons.

source: The Dunmore transit board voted 6 to 3 on Tuesday to eliminate bus fares for riders under 18 and over 65, starting 1 January. Currently, standard fares are 2.25 dollars, and the two groups account for about 21 percent of the 9.4 million trips taken each year. Board staff estimate the change will cost 1.7 million dollars in lost revenue annually, which will be covered by a new 0.1 percent increase in the regional sales tax approved by voters in 2022. Supporters said free fares would help families and reduce traffic near schools, while opponents argued that the money should go toward more frequent service on busy routes. The board will review ridership data after one year and may adjust the policy if costs exceed projections.
target_summary: Dunmore's transit board voted to eliminate bus fares for youths and seniors.

source: Visitors to the island of Valmora can reach it by ferry from the port of Sestri, a crossing that takes 95 minutes and costs 28 euros each way. Boats leave at 8:00, 12:30, and 17:00 daily from May to September, but only once a day in winter, and sailings are often canceled when winds exceed 40 knots. Once on the island, there are no cars allowed in the main village, so most travelers rent bicycles or walk the 6-kilometer coastal path to the lighthouse. Accommodation is limited to about 400 beds, and rooms in August are usually booked by March. Travelers who prefer a quieter trip should visit in late May or early October, when prices drop by roughly a third and the beaches are almost empty.
target_summary: Valmora island is reached by a 95-minute ferry from Sestri.

source: Psychologists who study habit formation have found that repeating an action in a stable context is more important than how motivated a person feels. In a well-known 2009 study, volunteers who tried to adopt a new daily behavior, such as eating a piece of fruit after lunch, took an average of 66 days for it to become automatic, although individual times ranged from 18 to 254 days. Missing a single day did not significantly harm the process, which suggests that occasional lapses are not a reason to give up. Researchers advise attaching the new behavior to an existing cue, for example doing ten push-ups right after brushing teeth, and keeping the first version of the habit so small that it feels almost too easy.
target_summary: Habits form through repetition in stable contexts, averaging 66 days.

source: The Aldermoor Suspension Bridge opened in 1931 after four years of construction and cost 5.8 million dollars, roughly twice the original estimate. Spanning 740 meters across the Teller River, it was briefly the longest suspension bridge in the country and became a symbol of the region's recovery from the previous decade's floods. Chief engineer Ruth Halvorsen insisted on testing the cables with a load 50 percent heavier than expected, a decision that later saved the structure when an overloaded convoy of trucks crossed it during the 1944 evacuation. By the 1990s corrosion had weakened several cables, and a two-year restoration project completed in 1998 replaced them without closing the bridge to traffic. Today it carries about 38,000 vehicles per day and is protected as a national landmark.
target_summary: The Aldermoor Suspension Bridge, opened in 1931, still carries heavy traffic.

source: Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium and supports bone strength, and most people produce it when their skin is exposed to sunlight. People who live far from the equator, spend most of their time indoors, or have darker skin may produce less and can develop low levels, particularly in winter. Foods such as fatty fish, egg yolks, and fortified milk supply smaller amounts. Health agencies commonly set the recommended daily intake at 600 international units for adults up to age 70 and 800 for older adults. Taking far more than this is not helpful and can be harmful, since excess vitamin D can raise blood calcium and cause nausea and kidney problems. Anyone who suspects a deficiency should ask a doctor for a blood test before starting high-dose supplements.
target_summary: Vitamin D supports calcium absorption; adults need 600 international units daily.

source: Code review is most effective when changes are small. A study of 2,500 reviews at a mid-sized software company found that pull requests under 200 lines were approved within four hours on average, while those over 800 lines took more than two days and received far fewer comments per line. Reviewers also missed more defects in large changes, apparently because fatigue set in after about an hour. The company responded by asking developers to split work into focused commits, adding automated checks for formatting and tests so humans could concentrate on design and logic, and setting a goal that every review begin within one working day. After six months, the average time to merge fell from 52 hours to 19, and production incidents linked to new code dropped by about a fifth.
target_summary: Small pull requests get reviewed faster and with fewer missed defects.

source: The Hollis Museum of Modern Art opens a retrospective of painter Ines Carvalho on 14 February, featuring 120 works created between 1968 and 2019. Carvalho, who is now 84, began as a figurative painter in Porto before shifting to large abstract canvases in the 1980s, using layers of translucent oil to produce glowing fields of color. The exhibition is organized in chronological order across five galleries and includes sketchbooks, letters, and a reconstruction of her studio. Curator Samuel Adeyemi said the show aims to correct the impression that she was a purely abstract painter, since her late works return to portraits of her neighbors. Tickets cost 18 dollars, and the exhibit runs until 28 September, with free admission on the first Sunday of every month.
target_summary: Hollis Museum opens an Ines Carvalho retrospective on 14 February.

source: Inflation measures how quickly the general level of prices rises over time, and it is usually reported as an annual percentage. If inflation is 4 percent, an item that cost 100 dollars last year now costs about 104 dollars. Central banks typically aim for a low and stable rate, often around 2 percent, because moderate inflation encourages spending and investment while avoiding the risks of falling prices. When inflation climbs too high, central banks raise interest rates to make borrowing more expensive and slow demand. This approach can work, but it takes months to take effect and can lead to job losses if rates rise too quickly. Households are affected unevenly: people on fixed incomes and those with savings in low-interest accounts lose purchasing power, while borrowers with fixed-rate loans benefit.
target_summary: Inflation is rising prices; central banks target about 2 percent.

source: Earthquake safety experts advise people to drop, cover, and hold on during shaking rather than running outside, because most injuries occur when people are struck by falling objects while moving. Inside a building, the safest place is under a sturdy desk or table, or against an interior wall away from windows. After the shaking stops, residents should check for injuries, turn off gas if they smell a leak, and expect aftershocks, which can continue for days. Every household should keep a kit with at least three days of water, at 4 liters per person per day, plus food, a flashlight, a radio, and any necessary medicines. Families are encouraged to practice their plan twice a year and to agree on a meeting place outside the home.
target_summary: During earthquakes, drop, cover, and hold on; keep emergency kits.

source: The Orlen Observatory announced in April that its new 2.4-meter telescope has captured the first clear images of the Veil Nebula's western arc since a major upgrade of its camera. The project took five years and cost 63 million dollars, most of it paid by a consortium of three universities. Astronomers expect the instrument to survey about 40,000 galaxies each year, nearly triple the output of the older telescope it replaces. Engineer Priya Nambiar said the main challenge was keeping the mirror at a steady temperature, which required a cooling system that adjusts every 30 seconds. The observatory sits at 3,100 meters in the Atacama Desert, where over 300 nights per year are cloudless. Public viewing nights will begin in June, with 60 tickets available each Friday.
target_summary: Orlen Observatory's new 2.4-meter telescope has captured first clear Veil Nebula images.

source: A vaccination campaign in the province of Talisay reached 91 percent of children under five in 2023, up from 68 percent three years earlier. Health workers credited the increase to mobile clinics that visited remote villages every second month and to text message reminders sent to parents a week before each appointment. The program also trained 140 volunteers to explain vaccine safety and to address rumors, which had been a leading cause of refusals. Measles cases in the province dropped from 212 in 2021 to just 9 in 2023. Officials caution that the gains could be lost if funding ends, since the mobile clinics cost 480,000 dollars per year. The provincial health office has asked the national government to renew its grant for another five years.
target_summary: Talisay's child vaccination coverage rose from 68 to 91 percent.

source: The novelist Adaeze Okonkwo published her debut, The Salt Merchant's Daughter, in 2016 after working for a decade as a court interpreter in Lagos. The book follows a young woman who inherits a failing trading business and must choose between selling it to a powerful rival and rebuilding it with her late father's loyal workers. Critics praised the clear prose and the portrayal of port life, though some thought the final third relied on coincidence. It sold more than 400,000 copies, won the Marlow Prize for first fiction, and was translated into 19 languages. A television adaptation, with Okonkwo as a producer, is scheduled to begin filming next spring. She is currently finishing a second novel set among fishermen in the Niger Delta.
target_summary: Adaeze Okonkwo's debut novel The Salt Merchant's Daughter sold over 400,000 copies.

source: Engineers at the Brennan Institute have developed a battery for electric buses that can recharge in eight minutes, compared with the three hours needed by current models. The design replaces the standard graphite anode with a silicon composite, which allows lithium ions to move faster but tends to swell and crack over time. To solve this problem, the team added a flexible polymer layer that absorbs the expansion. In laboratory tests, the battery kept 87 percent of its capacity after 2,000 charging cycles. A pilot fleet of ten buses will begin carrying passengers in the city of Halden in September. If the trial succeeds, the institute plans to license the technology to manufacturers and hopes to see commercial production by 2028.
target_summary: Brennan Institute's silicon-anode bus battery recharges in eight minutes.

source: Under the new Tenant Protection Act, which takes effect on 1 July, landlords in the province must give at least 90 days of written notice before raising rent, up from 30 days. Annual increases are capped at 5 percent unless the landlord can show that major repairs justify a higher amount, in which case a tribunal must approve the change. Tenants who are evicted without a valid reason can claim compensation equal to three months of rent. Landlords' groups argue that the cap will discourage investment in new housing, while tenant advocates say that rents have risen 22 percent in three years and that families are being forced to leave their neighborhoods. The government will review the law after two years and publish data on vacancy rates and construction permits.
target_summary: The Tenant Protection Act requires 90 days' notice for rent increases.

source: Bread made with a sourdough starter rises more slowly than yeast bread, but many bakers prefer its tangy flavor and chewy crust. A starter is a mixture of flour and water in which wild yeast and bacteria grow together, and it must be fed regularly with fresh flour to stay active. A typical routine is to discard half of the starter each day and replace it with equal weights of flour and water. A new starter usually becomes reliable after about seven to ten days, when it doubles in size within six hours of feeding. Dough made with it needs a long fermentation, often twelve hours at room temperature, followed by baking in a preheated Dutch oven at 230 degrees Celsius to produce a crisp, golden crust.
target_summary: Sourdough uses a regularly fed starter and long fermentation for tangy flavor.

source: The city of Riverton has approved a plan to convert a four-kilometer stretch of unused railway into a linear park with a bicycle path, community gardens, and a performance stage. Construction will start in March and is expected to take two years, with a budget of 27 million dollars, half of which comes from a federal grant. Residents in the surrounding neighborhoods, who have fewer parks than any other part of the city, were consulted in 14 public meetings before the final design was chosen. Some property owners are concerned that rents will rise once the park opens, and the council has promised to set aside 15 percent of new housing nearby as affordable units. The first section, about one kilometer long, should open to visitors by next autumn.
target_summary: Riverton will turn an unused four-kilometer railway into a linear park.

source: Rust forms when iron reacts with oxygen in the presence of water, producing a reddish compound called iron oxide. The process is a type of electrochemical reaction: in one part of the metal surface, iron atoms lose electrons and dissolve into the water, while in another part oxygen gains those electrons. Salt speeds up the reaction because it makes the water better at conducting electricity, which is why cars rust faster in places where roads are salted in winter. Rust is weaker and more brittle than iron and flakes away, exposing fresh metal beneath it. Common ways to prevent it include painting the surface, coating it with zinc in a process called galvanizing, or mixing chromium into the iron to make stainless steel.
target_summary: Rust forms when iron reacts with oxygen and water.

source: A survey of 1,800 office workers across six countries found that employees who work from home two or three days each week reported higher job satisfaction than those who work entirely in the office or entirely at home. Fully remote workers said they felt more isolated and less likely to be considered for promotion, while full-time office workers cited long commutes, which averaged 54 minutes each way, as their biggest frustration. Managers surveyed by the same team said that productivity was similar across all three arrangements, but that new employees learned faster when they spent at least three days a week in person. The authors suggest that companies set clear expectations about which days are shared in the office, instead of leaving the schedule to each individual.
target_summary: Hybrid workers reported higher job satisfaction than fully remote or office workers.

source: The Marenko String Quartet will perform the complete Beethoven quartets over eight concerts between October and May at the Wellington Concert Hall. Founded in 1998, the ensemble has recorded all sixteen of the works twice, and their second set, released in 2019, received a major international award. Each concert will pair one late quartet with an early or middle work, so that audiences can hear how the composer's style changed over time. The first violinist, Katarina Lund, said that preparing the cycle has taken three years of rehearsals, including a month of study in Vienna. Subscriptions for the whole series cost 320 dollars, while individual tickets start at 45 dollars. Students can attend any concert for 10 dollars at the door.
target_summary: The Marenko String Quartet will perform all Beethoven quartets in eight concerts.

source: Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor but support about a quarter of all marine species, making them one of the most diverse habitats on Earth. They are built by tiny animals called polyps, which live in partnership with algae that give them color and provide most of their food through photosynthesis. When the water becomes too warm, polyps expel the algae, and the coral turns white in a process known as bleaching. Corals can recover if temperatures fall quickly, but repeated or prolonged bleaching often kills them. A marine survey in 2023 estimated that 14 percent of the world's coral had died in the previous decade, mostly due to rising sea temperatures. Scientists are testing heat-tolerant strains that could be planted on damaged reefs.
target_summary: Coral reefs, rich in species, are dying from warming-induced bleaching.

source: The regional grocery chain Fairmont Markets announced that it will close 12 of its 85 stores by the end of the year, citing weak sales and rising rent. Chief financial officer Jorge Alvarez said that the affected locations have lost money for three consecutive years, and that about 480 employees will be offered positions at nearby stores or severance packages worth up to eight weeks of pay. The company plans to invest the savings in a home delivery service, which currently accounts for only 4 percent of its revenue, and in upgrades to its remaining stores. Analysts said that the move reflects a broader trend, as customers increasingly buy groceries online or from discount chains. Shares of Fairmont rose 3 percent after the announcement.
target_summary: Fairmont Markets will close 12 of its 85 stores.

source: Gregor Mendel, an Austrian monk, discovered the basic rules of inheritance by breeding pea plants in the garden of his monastery between 1856 and 1863. He studied seven traits, including seed shape and flower color, and tracked them across thousands of plants. When he crossed plants with purple flowers and plants with white flowers, all the offspring had purple flowers, but when he bred those offspring together, about three quarters were purple and one quarter were white. From this pattern he concluded that each trait is controlled by two units, now called alleles, and that one can be dominant over the other. His work was published in 1866 but was largely ignored until 1900, when three scientists independently rediscovered his results.
target_summary: Gregor Mendel discovered inheritance rules by breeding pea plants.

source: Phishing emails remain the most common way that attackers gain access to company networks, accounting for about 36 percent of breaches in a 2023 industry report. These messages often imitate a trusted sender, such as a bank or a manager, and urge the recipient to click a link or open an attachment immediately. Warning signs include a sender address that differs slightly from the real one, spelling mistakes, and unexpected requests for passwords or payments. Security experts recommend that employees hover over links to check the true address before clicking, report suspicious messages to the IT department, and use multi-factor authentication so that a stolen password alone is not enough. Companies that run regular training exercises have reduced the rate of clicks on fake phishing emails from 30 percent to under 5 percent.
target_summary: Phishing causes about 36 percent of breaches; training and multi-factor authentication help.

source: Researchers at the University of Kellan reported that a common soil bacterium can break down certain plastics at room temperature. The team found that the microbe, named Pseudomonas kellanensis, digested about 12 percent of a polyethylene film over six weeks when given no other source of carbon. Although the rate is too slow for industrial use, the scientists identified the enzyme responsible and are now trying to improve it through genetic engineering. Dr. Haruto Mizuno, the lead author, stressed that plastic waste should still be reduced at the source, since even a faster enzyme would need years of development. The paper appeared in the journal Applied Microbiology and was funded by a grant of 1.4 million dollars from the national science agency.
target_summary: A soil bacterium can digest polyethylene plastic at room temperature.

source: In small towns, local newspapers have traditionally acted as a record of community life, covering school boards, zoning hearings, and high school sports. Since 2005, however, more than one fifth of the country's newspapers have closed, leaving about 200 counties with no local news source at all. Studies of these so-called news deserts show that voter turnout falls and that municipal borrowing costs rise, probably because there is less scrutiny of public spending. Some communities have responded by launching nonprofit news sites, which rely on donations and foundation grants instead of advertising. One example is the Harbor Courier, founded in 2019 with four reporters, which now has 6,500 paying members and has uncovered misuse of funds at the local water district.
target_summary: Local newspaper closures create news deserts, lowering turnout; nonprofit sites respond.

source: The Selene-3 lander touched down near the lunar south pole on 18 November after a six-day journey from Earth. The mission, led by the Meridian Space Agency with partners in four countries, carries a drill that can collect samples from up to one meter below the surface and a set of instruments to search for frozen water. Mission controllers confirmed that the lander is stable and that its solar panels are generating 480 watts, enough to power the equipment during the lunar day. The two-week operation will end when the long lunar night begins and temperatures fall below minus 170 degrees Celsius, which the craft is not designed to survive. Scientists expect the first drilling results within ten days and hope to publish an analysis before the end of next year.
target_summary: The Selene-3 lander touched down near the lunar south pole.

source: Regular physical activity has been shown to reduce symptoms of mild to moderate depression, with effects similar in size to those of some medications in short-term studies. A review of 41 trials involving more than 2,900 adults found that three sessions of aerobic exercise per week, lasting 30 to 45 minutes, produced the largest improvements. Researchers believe that exercise may help by raising levels of brain chemicals that regulate mood, improving sleep, and giving people a sense of achievement and social contact. However, the authors note that many of the trials were small and that people with severe depression need professional treatment. They recommend that patients talk to a doctor before starting a new exercise program, and that they choose activities they enjoy, because people are more likely to continue them.
target_summary: Aerobic exercise reduces mild to moderate depression symptoms.

source: The Delmar factory in the city of Ostrava switched to a four-day workweek in January, with employees working ten hours a day from Monday to Thursday. The 320 workers kept their full salaries, and management expected output to fall by about five percent. Instead, production rose by 3 percent in the first six months, absenteeism dropped by nearly a third, and the number of workplace accidents fell from 17 to 9. Supervisors said that workers were more alert at the start of each shift and that the three-day weekend reduced fatigue. However, some employees with young children found the long days difficult, and the company has set up a subsidized childcare program that opens at 6 a.m. It will decide in December whether to make the change permanent.
target_summary: Delmar's four-day workweek raised production 3 percent and cut absenteeism.

source: Lake Baikal, in southern Siberia, is the deepest lake in the world, reaching 1,642 meters at its lowest point, and it holds about one fifth of the planet's unfrozen fresh water. It is also thought to be the oldest lake, having formed roughly 25 million years ago in a rift in the Earth's crust. The lake is home to more than 1,700 species of plants and animals, of which about two thirds are found nowhere else, including the Baikal seal, one of the few freshwater seals. In winter, the surface freezes to a thickness of up to a meter, and the ice is strong enough for vehicles to cross. Pollution from nearby factories and tourism has raised concerns, and the lake has been a World Heritage Site since 1996.
target_summary: Lake Baikal is the world's deepest and oldest lake.

The route was made possible by a new bilateral agreement that doubled the number of weekly flights allowed between the two countries. Airline executives said that demand from tourists and from Japanese manufacturers with plants in the Visayas had grown steadily since 2022. Passengers will travel in a single economy cabin, but a limited number of seats with extra legroom will be sold for a fee of 25 dollars. Flight times will be about four hours and ten minutes.
target_summary: Skyline Air will fly Cebu-Osaka nonstop four times weekly from 3 March, with fares from 210 dollars, after a new bilateral agreement.

source: Prescribed burning is the deliberate use of low-intensity fire to remove dry brush and fallen branches from a forest floor before they can fuel a larger wildfire. In the Calloway National Forest, crews carried out burns on 9,400 hectares last spring, nearly twice the area treated in the previous year. Burns are scheduled only when humidity is above 30 percent and winds are below 15 kilometers per hour, which keeps the flames small and easy to control. Studies show that treated areas suffer about 60 percent less damage when a wildfire later reaches them. The practice has critics, however, because smoke can aggravate asthma, and a few burns have escaped control. Forest managers now notify nearby residents 48 hours in advance and monitor air quality during every operation.
target_summary: Prescribed burns in Calloway National Forest reduce wildfire fuel.

source: Antibiotic resistance occurs when bacteria evolve ways to survive drugs that once killed them. Every use of an antibiotic gives resistant bacteria a chance to multiply while sensitive ones die, so the more the drugs are used, the faster resistance spreads. Doctors estimate that about a third of antibiotic prescriptions for respiratory infections are unnecessary, since most of those illnesses are caused by viruses, against which antibiotics have no effect. A 2022 analysis linked drug-resistant infections to roughly 1.2 million deaths worldwide in a single year. To slow the problem, health agencies urge patients to take antibiotics only when prescribed, to finish the full course, and never to share leftover pills. Hospitals are also tightening hygiene rules, and researchers are searching for new classes of drugs.
target_summary: Antibiotic overuse spreads bacterial resistance, so use only when prescribed.

source: Online retailer Brightcart said on Monday that it will replace plastic mailers with recycled paper envelopes for all orders under two kilograms by the end of June. The change will affect about 11 million parcels per year and is expected to cut the company's plastic use by 900 tonnes. Customer surveys found that 58 percent of shoppers care about packaging waste, but the company warned that paper costs about 12 percent more and may add a few cents to some deliveries. Brightcart also plans to expand its return program, in which customers can drop off unwanted items at partner stores instead of mailing them back, reducing delivery trips. Environmental groups welcomed the announcement but urged the company to publish annual data so that its claims can be verified.
target_summary: Brightcart will replace plastic mailers with recycled paper envelopes by June.

source: Divers exploring the Gulf of Teras have found the remains of a merchant ship that sank around 1450 BCE, making it one of the oldest known shipwrecks in the region. The vessel, about 15 meters long, lay at a depth of 52 meters and carried a cargo of roughly 300 copper ingots and several hundred pottery jars. Team leader Dr. Maria Constantin said that the well-preserved timbers will help researchers understand how ships were built in the late Bronze Age. The discovery was made in August using an underwater robot that mapped the site in three dimensions before any objects were disturbed. The ingots, which weigh about 25 kilograms each, were probably mined on the nearby island of Kyrelia. Recovery of the cargo is planned for next summer.
target_summary: Divers found a 1450 BCE merchant shipwreck carrying copper ingots.

source: The Northreach offshore wind farm, which began delivering power in May, consists of 62 turbines located 18 kilometers from the coast. Each turbine is 220 meters tall and can generate 12 megawatts, giving the project a total capacity of 744 megawatts, enough to supply about 700,000 homes. The 2.9 billion dollar development took four years to build and was financed by two pension funds and a utility company. Fishing groups initially objected to the project, so the developers agreed to leave wide corridors between turbine rows and to pay 8 million dollars into a fund for local harbors. Operators say the turbines will run about 45 percent of the time at full output, and that maintenance crews will use a dedicated vessel based in the nearby port of Alden.
target_summary: The Northreach offshore wind farm now powers about 700,000 homes.

source: Of the roughly 7,000 languages spoken in the world, about 40 percent are considered endangered, meaning that they have few young speakers. A language is usually in danger when children stop learning it at home, since it then depends on a shrinking generation of elders. Revitalization efforts have succeeded in a few places: in New Zealand, immersion preschools known as language nests have helped raise the number of Maori speakers, and in Wales, bilingual education is credited with reversing decades of decline. Experts say that successful programs share three features: strong community leadership, support from government funding, and regular opportunities for young people to use the language outside school. Digital tools such as dictionaries and mobile apps can help, but they cannot replace daily conversation.
target_summary: About 40 percent of the world's 7,000 languages are endangered.

source: The Mjolby Tower, completed in 2022, is an 18-story office building in Stockholm whose structure is made almost entirely of engineered timber. Its columns and floors use cross-laminated timber, a material made of wooden boards glued in alternating layers, which is strong enough to support tall buildings while being much lighter than concrete. The architects estimate that the design saved about 2,800 tonnes of carbon dioxide compared with a conventional building of the same size, since trees absorb the gas as they grow. Fire safety was a major concern, but thick timber chars on the outside and protects the inner wood, and the building also has sprinklers in every room. Construction took 14 months, about a quarter less than a similar concrete tower, because most parts were prefabricated in a factory.
target_summary: Stockholm's Mjolby Tower is an 18-story timber office building.

source: The Hartwell Foundation will award 200 full scholarships in the coming academic year to students from rural districts who plan to study engineering or nursing. Each scholarship covers tuition, housing, and a monthly allowance of 150 dollars for up to four years, as long as the student maintains a grade average of at least 80 percent. Applicants must have a family income below the national median and complete an essay and an interview. The foundation, created in 2009 by a retired shipping executive, has so far supported 1,100 graduates, of whom 86 percent found work in their field within six months. Applications open on 1 December and close on 15 February, and recipients will be announced in April. Information sessions will be held in 30 towns.
target_summary: Hartwell Foundation offers 200 full scholarships to rural engineering and nursing students.

source: Harvest Valley Foods has recalled 48,000 jars of its roasted peanut spread after tests detected salmonella in a sample from one production line. The affected jars carry best-before dates between 4 August and 30 October and were sold in 11 states through supermarkets and online. So far, 27 people have reported illness linked to the product, and six were hospitalized, but no deaths have been confirmed. Health officials urge consumers to check their pantries, throw away any recalled jars or return them for a refund, and wash surfaces that touched the product. The company has suspended production at the plant while inspectors investigate how the contamination occurred. It said that it will install additional testing equipment and publish the results of the inquiry within 60 days.
target_summary: Harvest Valley Foods recalled 48,000 peanut spread jars over salmonella.

source: Hotel occupancy in the coastal city of Marbella Bay reached 84 percent in July, the highest monthly rate since records began in 2004, according to the local tourism board. The average nightly price rose 11 percent to 143 euros, and visitors spent an estimated 96 million euros on accommodation, dining, and activities. Officials attributed the surge to new direct flights from five European cities and to a promotional campaign aimed at families. The boom has created pressure, however: residents complain of crowded beaches and rising rents, and the council is considering a tourist tax of two euros per night to pay for cleaning and public transport. Hotel owners oppose the measure, arguing that it could drive visitors to neighboring towns, but a vote is expected in October.
target_summary: Marbella Bay's July hotel occupancy hit a record 84 percent.

source: The trolley problem is a famous thought experiment in ethics, introduced by philosopher Philippa Foot in 1967. In its basic form, a runaway trolley will kill five people on the track unless you pull a lever that sends it onto a side track, where it will kill one person. Most people say it is acceptable to pull the lever. In a variation by Judith Jarvis Thomson, however, the only way to stop the trolley is to push a large man off a bridge into its path, and far fewer people approve, even though the numbers are the same. Philosophers use the contrast to examine whether the morality of an action depends only on its outcomes, or also on factors such as intention and direct physical harm.
target_summary: The trolley problem tests whether morality depends only on outcomes.

source: The startup Voxel Labs has released a speech recognition system that it says transcribes meetings with a word error rate of 4.8 percent, compared with 7.1 percent for the leading competitor. The company trained the model on 90,000 hours of recordings in 14 languages, including accented English and conversations with several speakers talking over each other. In independent tests by the Aldridge Speech Group, the system performed well in quiet rooms but its error rate rose to 11 percent in noisy cafes. Voxel plans to offer the product through a subscription priced at 12 dollars per user per month, with a free tier limited to five hours of audio. Privacy advocates have asked the firm to clarify whether customer recordings are used for further training, and the company promised to publish a policy next month.
target_summary: Voxel Labs' speech recognition achieves a 4.8 percent word error rate.

source: Meteorologists forecast that this year's monsoon will bring rainfall about 6 percent above the long-term average to the western coast, after two consecutive seasons of below-normal rain. The prediction is based on warm ocean temperatures in the Indian Ocean and on the absence of an El Nino, which usually weakens the monsoon. Farmers, who rely on the rains for roughly half of the country's crops, have been advised to plant rice and pulses earlier than usual. Heavy rain also carries risks: the weather agency warned that coastal and low-lying districts may face flooding in July and August, and it has set up a text message alert system that reaches 40 million subscribers. Authorities urge local governments to clear drains before the season starts.
target_summary: This year's monsoon is forecast to bring above-average western coast rainfall.

source: After a decade of overfishing, the Strait of Corvan cod fishery was closed entirely in 2014, when the estimated population had fallen to 11 percent of its historic level. A recovery plan introduced strict annual catch limits, banned the use of fine-mesh nets that trap juvenile fish, and set up three no-fishing zones around spawning grounds. Scientists reported in March that the cod population has risen to about 38 percent of its historic size, and the fishery reopened in 2021 with a quota of 4,000 tonnes. Fishers who accepted the cuts initially lost income, but a government buyback program compensated them for retiring 60 older boats. Researchers warn that the recovery is still fragile and that raising quotas too quickly could undo the progress.
target_summary: Corvan cod recovered from 11 to 38 percent of historic levels.

source: The share of adults in Kenvale who use mobile payments rose from 31 percent in 2019 to 74 percent last year, according to a central bank survey of 12,000 households. Growth was fastest among small traders, such as market vendors, 62 percent of whom now accept payments by phone, compared with 9 percent before the pandemic. The central bank plans to require stronger identity checks and to fund a financial literacy campaign in 200 villages.

source: Every October, the people of the mountain town of Quillan gather for the Festival of Lanterns, a three-day celebration that marks the end of the potato harvest. On the first night, families carry paper lanterns to the cemetery to honor their ancestors, and they leave food and flowers beside the graves. The second day is devoted to a market where farmers sell more than forty varieties of native potatoes, and musicians play traditional flutes and drums. On the final evening, residents release hundreds of lanterns into the sky from the central plaza. Anthropologists who study the event say it strengthens community ties and preserves agricultural knowledge. Attendance has grown from 2,000 in 2010 to more than 25,000, prompting the town to limit visitor numbers and require advance registration.
target_summary: Quillan's three-day Festival of Lanterns marks the potato harvest's end.

source: A superconductor is a material that conducts electricity with no resistance when cooled below a critical temperature, so a current can flow through it indefinitely without losing energy. The phenomenon was discovered in 1911 by Heike Kamerlingh Onnes, who observed it in mercury cooled to about four kelvin, close to absolute zero. Superconductors also expel magnetic fields, which allows a magnet to float above one. Today they are used to build the powerful electromagnets in magnetic resonance imaging scanners and in particle accelerators. The main obstacle to wider use is the need for extreme cooling, usually with liquid helium or liquid nitrogen. Researchers are searching for materials that superconduct at room temperature, but none has been confirmed, and several widely publicized claims have failed to hold up under independent testing.
target_summary: Superconductors conduct electricity without resistance below a critical temperature.

source: Lithium-ion batteries in smartphones wear out gradually, and the way a phone is charged can make the difference between lasting two years or four. Heat is the biggest enemy, so it is best to avoid leaving the device in direct sunlight or in a hot car. Keeping the charge between 20 and 80 percent reduces stress on the battery, whereas frequently draining it to zero or holding it at 100 percent for long periods speeds up aging. Many phones now include a setting that pauses charging at 80 percent and finishes just before the owner wakes up. Fast charging is safe for occasional use, but slower chargers generate less heat. Manufacturers typically say a battery should keep about 80 percent of its original capacity after 500 full cycles.
target_summary: Avoid heat and keep phone charge between 20 and 80 percent.

source: The Eastside Community Food Bank distributed 1.9 million kilograms of food last year, a 35 percent increase over the previous year, as the number of households seeking help rose to 14,500. About three quarters of the food came from grocery stores and farms that donate surplus products, while the remainder was purchased with donations. Executive director Fatima Rahman said that more working families are visiting, many of whom had never needed assistance before, because of higher rents and food prices. The organization relies on 620 volunteers, who sort and pack boxes every Tuesday and Saturday. To meet demand, it is raising 2.5 million dollars to buy a refrigerated warehouse, which would allow it to accept more fresh produce and dairy. So far, 1.6 million dollars has been pledged.

source: Mount Arkane, a volcano on the island of Sorrel, erupted on 12 March after 140 years of silence, sending an ash plume 9 kilometers into the sky. Authorities had raised the alert level two weeks earlier, when sensors detected a swarm of small earthquakes and a swelling of the summit, and they evacuated 18,000 residents from towns within 10 kilometers of the crater. No deaths were reported, and officials credited the early warning system, which had been installed in 2016 with funding from the United Nations. Flights to the island were suspended for four days because ash can damage jet engines. Volcanologists say the eruption is likely to continue in smaller bursts for several weeks, and evacuees are not expected to return home before the end of April.
target_summary: Mount Arkane erupted on 12 March, prompting 18,000 evacuations.

source: The game of chess is believed to have originated in India around the sixth century, where an early version called chaturanga featured pieces representing the infantry, cavalry, elephants, and chariots of an army. It spread to Persia and then, after the Arab conquests, to Europe, where by about 1475 the queen and bishop had gained their modern powers, making the game much faster. The first official world championship took place in 1886, and Wilhelm Steinitz became the first recognized champion. In 1997, the computer Deep Blue defeated world champion Garry Kasparov in a six-game match, the first time a machine beat a reigning champion under tournament conditions. Today engines are far stronger than any human, and players use them to study openings and analyze games.
target_summary: Chess originated in India around the sixth century.

source: Flood damage is excluded from most standard home insurance policies, so homeowners in risk areas usually need a separate flood policy. In the Pelham district, where rivers flooded twice in the past decade, only 29 percent of households have such coverage, according to a 2024 survey by the insurance regulator. Premiums average 840 dollars per year, but they can exceed 3,000 dollars for houses close to the water. Many residents say they did not know that their existing policies excluded flooding until they filed claims. Regulators now require insurers to put a clear notice on the first page of every home policy, and the government is considering a subsidy for low-income families. Experts advise homeowners to check the flood risk map for their address and to remember that coverage usually begins only after a 30-day waiting period.
target_summary: Homeowners in risk areas need separate flood insurance.

source: Tooth decay begins when bacteria in the mouth feed on sugars and produce acids that dissolve the hard enamel covering each tooth. At first the damage is invisible, but over time it creates a hole called a cavity, which can reach the sensitive inner layers and cause pain or infection. Dentists recommend brushing twice a day for two minutes with a fluoride toothpaste, because fluoride helps enamel repair itself, and cleaning between the teeth once a day with floss or small brushes. Limiting sugary drinks is equally important, since frequent sipping keeps the mouth acidic for hours. Regular checkups, usually every six months, allow dentists to find decay early, when it can often be treated with a small filling instead of a root canal or an extraction.
target_summary: Sugar-feeding bacteria cause cavities; brushing with fluoride toothpaste prevents them.

source: The Penny Post, introduced in Britain in 1840, transformed the way people communicated by allowing a letter to be sent anywhere in the country for a flat charge of one penny. Before the reform, postage was calculated by distance and paid by the recipient, which made letters too expensive for most workers and encouraged people to refuse delivery. Educator Rowland Hill, who proposed the change, also suggested that senders pay in advance with an adhesive label, leading to the first postage stamp, the Penny Black. In the first year, the number of letters handled rose from about 76 million to 169 million. The system was copied by dozens of countries within two decades, and it is considered a forerunner of modern universal postal services.
target_summary: Britain's 1840 Penny Post allowed letters anywhere for one penny.

source: Sales of dedicated digital cameras have fallen by more than 80 percent since their peak in 2010, as smartphones have taken over casual photography. The industry has responded by focusing on premium products: mirrorless cameras with large sensors now account for most of the revenue, and the average price has risen from about 400 dollars to nearly 1,200. Manufacturers say that professionals and serious hobbyists still prefer these models for their image quality, interchangeable lenses, and manual controls. Meanwhile, smartphone makers have narrowed the gap using software that combines several exposures into a single image. Analysts expect camera sales to stay flat for the next five years, with growth coming mainly from video creators who want sharper footage than a phone can provide.
target_summary: Dedicated camera sales fell over 80 percent since 2010 as smartphones rose.

source: The city of Ravenna Heights launched a bicycle sharing program in April with 1,500 bikes at 200 docking stations spread across the downtown and university districts. A single ride costs 1.50 dollars for the first 30 minutes, and monthly passes are available for 18 dollars. In the first six months, riders took 840,000 trips, with the busiest hours falling between 8 and 9 a.m. and 5 and 6 p.m., which suggests that most people use the bikes for commuting. Surveys show that 22 percent of users previously drove or took a taxi for the same journey. The program has faced problems, including theft of 140 bicycles and complaints that stations are scarce in lower-income neighborhoods. The city has promised 60 new stations in those areas by next year.

source: The Carvena Aqueduct, built by Roman engineers around 40 CE, carried water 52 kilometers from mountain springs to the port city of Carvena, descending only 170 meters along its entire length. This gentle slope of about one part in 300 was achieved by surveyors using simple instruments and by building tunnels, channels, and a three-tiered stone bridge 38 meters high across the Ostra valley. At its peak, the aqueduct supplied roughly 20,000 cubic meters of water per day to public fountains, bathhouses, and wealthy homes. source: Results of the national census released this week show that the population of Valdora reached 11.3 million, an increase of 6 percent since the last count ten years ago. Detailed regional data will be published in March.

source: The spacing effect is one of the most reliable findings in the psychology of learning: information studied in several short sessions spread over days or weeks is remembered much longer than the same material studied in a single marathon session. In one experiment, students who reviewed vocabulary lists at intervals of one week retained about 80 percent after a month, whereas students who crammed retained only 30 percent. Researchers explain the effect by noting that each time a memory is retrieved after some forgetting, it becomes stronger and easier to recall in the future. Educators recommend that students practice testing themselves rather than rereading notes, and that they schedule reviews at expanding intervals, such as one day, three days, one week, and one month.
target_summary: Spaced study sessions produce longer-lasting memory than cramming.

source: Telecom operator Zenith Mobile completed the rollout of its 5G network in the capital region on 1 September, covering 91 percent of the population with 2,400 new base stations. The company spent 1.1 billion dollars on the project over three years and says that average download speeds have risen from 38 megabits per second on its older network to 310. Subscribers can access the new service at no extra charge, though only phones released after 2020 are compatible. Consumer groups welcomed the speeds but criticized the company for charging 12 percent more for its premium plans. Zenith plans to extend coverage to rural areas by 2027 with help from a government fund, and it expects 5G to account for more than half of its mobile subscribers by the end of next year.
target_summary: Zenith Mobile completed 5G coverage of 91 percent of the capital region.

source: The Lakeshore International Film Festival ended on Sunday after ten days, during which 142 films from 48 countries were screened for an audience of about 85,000. The top prize, the Golden Heron, went to The Last Ferry, a drama directed by Mirela Popescu about a family that runs a ferry service on a remote river. The jury, chaired by actor Daniel Osei, praised the film for its restrained storytelling and strong performances by non-professional actors. The audience award went to a documentary about community beekeepers in Ethiopia. Festival director Sophie Lambert said ticket sales were 17 percent higher than last year, and that organizers will add a fourth screening venue in 2025 to accommodate growing demand.
target_summary: The Golden Heron went to The Last Ferry.

source: Animal shelters in the Greater Mara region took in 21,000 dogs last year, and about 3,800 of them were euthanized because of overcrowding. Adopting a shelter dog can reduce this number, but experts advise prospective owners to prepare carefully. Before adoption, a family should consider the dog's size, energy level, and age, since young dogs need far more exercise and training than older ones. Adoption fees typically range from 50 to 200 dollars and usually include vaccinations and sterilization, which would otherwise cost more than 300 dollars. Shelter staff recommend a trial period of two weeks, called fostering, so that the dog and household can see whether they suit one another. Roughly one in ten adopted dogs is returned, most often because of behavior problems that could have been anticipated.
target_summary: Prospective owners should prepare carefully before adopting shelter dogs.

source: Demand for lithium, the key ingredient in electric vehicle batteries, is expected to grow fivefold by 2030, and mining companies are racing to open new sources. The Alvarado Salt Flat, high in the Andes, holds an estimated 8 million tonnes of lithium, and a new facility there will begin extracting it in 2026. The process pumps salty water into large ponds, where the sun evaporates it over 12 to 18 months, but it consumes enormous amounts of water in one of the driest regions on Earth. Indigenous communities nearby say their wells have started to run dry, and they have asked the government to suspend permits until independent studies are complete. The company has promised to use a new method that returns most of the water to the ground, though the technology has so far been tested only on a small scale.
target_summary: Lithium mining in the Andes threatens dry-region water supplies.

source: Rainwater harvesting, the practice of collecting rain from roofs and storing it in tanks, can supply households with water for gardening, laundry, and toilets, reducing the use of treated mains water by up to 50 percent. A typical system consists of gutters, a filter to remove leaves and debris, and a storage tank, which can hold anywhere from 200 liters in a simple barrel to 10,000 liters in a buried tank. In a region receiving 800 millimeters of rain a year, a 100-square-meter roof can collect about 64,000 liters annually, assuming 80 percent efficiency. Water intended for drinking must be treated with additional filtration and disinfection. Several cities now offer rebates of up to 500 dollars to homeowners who install tanks, because the practice also reduces stormwater runoff and flooding.
target_summary: Rainwater harvesting can cut mains water use by up to half.

source: A nursing home in the town of Oakmere has introduced a program that pairs residents with kindergarten children for weekly activities such as reading, painting, and gardening. Started in 2022 with 18 residents and 25 children, it has grown to 60 residents and 80 children. Staff members report that participating residents are more active and less likely to feel lonely, and records show that falls among them dropped by 15 percent during the first year. The children, who visit on Wednesday afternoons, have learned to interact comfortably with older people, according to teachers. The program costs about 9,000 dollars per year, mainly for transportation and materials, and is financed by a local community foundation. Similar projects are now being planned at four other care homes in the region.
target_summary: Oakmere's nursing home pairs residents with kindergarteners, reducing falls and loneliness.

source: Logistics company Stackline has deployed 450 autonomous robots at its distribution center in Raleigh, where they carry shelves of goods to human workers at packing stations instead of workers walking the aisles. Each robot is about the size of a small table, travels at 1.5 meters per second, and returns to a charging dock automatically when its battery runs low. The company says the system has doubled the number of orders processed per hour and reduced errors by 35 percent. The warehouse still employs 900 people, but the roles have shifted toward supervising the machines and handling items that need careful inspection. Labor unions have asked for guarantees that the technology will not lead to layoffs, and Stackline has said it will retrain any affected employees.
target_summary: Stackline's 450 warehouse robots doubled order processing and cut errors.

source: The Verrin Glacier in the Swiss Alps has lost about 30 percent of its volume since 1990, according to measurements published by a team from the Zurich Institute of Glaciology. Using laser scans from aircraft, the researchers found that the glacier's front has retreated 1.2 kilometers and that its surface is lowering by an average of one meter each year. Meltwater from glaciers feeds rivers that supply drinking water, farms, and hydroelectric dams, so the loss will eventually reduce summer water flows. In the short term, however, melting increases flows, creating a risk of flooding from lakes that form behind glacial debris. The team recommends installing sensors to monitor these lakes and developing plans to capture water in reservoirs. They predict that the glacier could disappear by 2100 if warming continues at current rates.
target_summary: Switzerland's Verrin Glacier has lost 30 percent of its volume since 1990.

source: Fast fashion companies produce clothing at low prices and in large volumes, releasing new styles as often as every week. The industry makes about 100 billion garments each year, and the average person buys 60 percent more clothing than 15 years ago while keeping each item for half as long. Textile waste is a growing concern: about 92 million tonnes are discarded annually, and less than one percent is recycled into new clothing, because blended fabrics are hard to separate. Some brands have introduced take-back programs and clothing made of recycled fibers, but critics say these efforts are small compared with total production. Researchers suggest that the most effective action for consumers is simply to buy less, choose durable items, and wear them longer, since extending a garment's life by nine months reduces its environmental impact by about 20 percent.
target_summary: Fast fashion drives textile waste; buying less and wearing longer helps.

source: A time bank is a community network in which members exchange services using hours of time instead of money. One hour of help, whether giving a ride, fixing a computer, or teaching a language, earns one time credit, which can be spent on an hour of someone else's help, regardless of the type of service. The idea was developed in the 1980s by law professor Edgar Cahn, and there are now more than 500 time banks in 40 countries. Studies of a time bank in Marlow with 900 members found that participants reported reduced isolation, and that retired members gained a sense of purpose. Critics note that time banks work best for simple tasks and struggle to supply professional services, such as plumbing or legal advice. Organizers say that they complement the economy rather than replace it.
target_summary: Time banks let members exchange services using hours instead of money.

source: The port of Sandhaven handled 3.8 million container units last year, a record that made it the busiest port on the southern coast. Congestion, however, has become a serious problem: ships waited an average of 2.6 days for a berth in the third quarter, compared with 0.9 days two years earlier. Port authorities blame a shortage of truck drivers and the fact that nearly a third of containers stay in the yard for more than a week. A 280 million dollar expansion, due to be finished in 2026, will add two berths and a rail terminal that can move 400,000 containers per year off the roads. In the meantime, the port has introduced a fee for containers left longer than five days, which has already cut average yard time by 18 percent.
target_summary: Sandhaven port handled a record 3.8 million containers amid worsening congestion.

Congestion, however, has become a serious problem: ships waited an average of 2.6 days for a berth in the third quarter, compared with 0.9 days two years earlier. Port authorities blame a shortage of truck drivers and the fact that nearly a third of containers stay in the yard for more than a week. A 280 million dollar expansion, due to be finished in 2026, will add two berths and a rail terminal that can move 400,000 containers per year off the roads. In the meantime, the port has introduced a fee for containers left longer than five days, which has already cut average yard time by 18 percent.
target_summary: Sandhaven port's record 3.8 million containers caused berth waits of 2.6 days; a 280 million dollar expansion and yard fees aim to help.

source: Wild bees and other insects pollinate about three quarters of the world's main food crops, including apples, almonds, and coffee, yet their numbers are declining in many regions. A long-term survey of 400 meadows across Europe found that the number of bumblebee species fell by 17 percent between 2005 and 2020. Researchers identify three main causes: the loss of flowering habitat because of intensive farming, the use of pesticides called neonicotinoids, and the spread of parasites. Some farmers have responded by planting strips of wildflowers along field edges, which increased bee visits by 50 percent in one trial. Scientists also recommend that gardeners plant a variety of native flowers that bloom at different times of the year, so that insects can find food from early spring until autumn.
target_summary: Pollinators are declining due to habitat loss, pesticides, and parasites.

source: A study of 42 hospitals in the Garrison Health Network found that each additional patient assigned to a nurse on a general ward was associated with a 7 percent increase in the risk of death within 30 days of surgery. The researchers examined records for 215,000 patients over four years and adjusted for age, illness severity, and type of operation. Hospitals where nurses cared for no more than five patients at a time also had shorter stays, averaging 4.1 days instead of 4.8. Hospital administrators say that nursing shortages make such staffing levels hard to reach, since about one in eight nursing positions in the network is vacant. The authors argue that the savings from fewer complications would offset much of the cost of hiring, and they recommend setting a maximum number of patients per nurse.
target_summary: More patients per nurse raised surgical death risk in hospitals.

source: Restoration workers at the Temple of Ankhara have uncovered a painted ceiling that was hidden for nearly 2,000 years behind a layer of soot and plaster. The paintings, which show a night sky with gold stars on a deep blue background, cover about 90 square meters of the main hall. Conservator Layla Haddad said that the pigments, which include a blue made from ground lapis lazuli, are in remarkably good condition because the plaster protected them from light and moisture. The restoration, which began in 2021 and has cost 3.5 million dollars, is expected to continue for another two years. Visitors will be able to view the ceiling from a raised walkway starting in spring, and daily entry will be limited to 600 people to protect the paintings.
target_summary: Restorers uncovered a 2,000-year-old painted star ceiling at Ankhara Temple.

source: The city of Brenton has voted to limit the number of rental electric scooters to 3,000 and to ban riding on sidewalks, after complaints about injuries and scooters left blocking pavements. Emergency rooms in the city treated 412 scooter-related injuries last year, nearly double the figure from the year before, and about half involved head injuries to riders who were not wearing helmets. Under the new rules, which take effect in May, companies must install a feature that slows scooters to 8 kilometers per hour in pedestrian zones and must pay a fine of 100 dollars for each scooter not removed from sidewalks within two hours. Scooter operators said the cap is too low, but riders' groups welcomed the creation of 40 kilometers of new protected lanes.
target_summary: Brenton capped rental scooters at 3,000 and banned sidewalk riding.

source: Hand hygiene is considered the single most effective way to prevent the spread of infections in hospitals, yet studies show that health workers clean their hands only about 40 percent of the times they should. The importance of handwashing was first demonstrated in 1847 by the Hungarian doctor Ignaz Semmelweis, who found that deaths among women giving birth in his ward fell from 18 percent to 2 percent after doctors began washing with chlorinated lime. Modern hospitals rely on alcohol-based hand rub, which works in 20 seconds and is placed at the entrance of every room. A recent campaign in 30 hospitals combined reminders, feedback from observers, and support from senior doctors, and it raised compliance from 48 to 71 percent, reducing bloodstream infections by about a fifth.
target_summary: Hand hygiene prevents hospital infections, but compliance remains low.

source: The spring climbing season on Mount Karaz ended last week with a record 612 climbers reaching the 7,940-meter summit, but it also brought the highest number of deaths in a decade, with nine climbers dying on the mountain. Guides said that a narrow window of good weather in late May sent hundreds of climbers up the final ridge on the same two days, creating dangerous queues at an altitude where each hour of delay increases the risk of exhaustion and frostbite. Authorities have proposed a daily limit of 150 permits and a requirement that climbers hire an experienced local guide. Mountain guides support the changes, but expedition companies warn that the limits may reduce income in a region where tourism provides about 30 percent of jobs.
target_summary: Karaz's record 612 summits came with nine deaths amid crowding.

source: Credit card interest is calculated on the balance that remains unpaid after the due date, and rates commonly range from 18 to 28 percent per year, far higher than most loans. If a cardholder pays the full statement balance every month, no interest is charged, thanks to a grace period of about 25 days on new purchases. However, paying only the minimum can be costly: a 3,000 dollar balance at 22 percent interest, paid down with only the minimum each month, can take many years to clear and cost thousands of dollars in interest. Financial counselors recommend paying as much as possible above the minimum, focusing first on the card with the highest rate, and avoiding cash advances, which usually carry extra fees and begin accruing interest immediately.
target_summary: Credit card interest is costly; pay full balances and avoid minimum-only payments.

source: Baking soda and baking powder are both chemical leavening agents, but they work differently. Baking soda is pure sodium bicarbonate, a base that needs an acidic ingredient, such as buttermilk, yogurt, honey, or lemon juice, to produce carbon dioxide bubbles. Baking powder contains baking soda plus a dry acid and a little cornstarch, so it reacts when it gets wet and again when it is heated, which makes it suitable for recipes without acidic ingredients. Using too much baking soda leaves a metallic, soapy taste, while too little yields dense baked goods. As a rule, a recipe uses about one teaspoon of baking powder for every cup of flour. Both ingredients lose strength over time, so bakers are advised to replace them every six months.
target_summary: Baking soda needs acid; baking powder contains its own acid.

source: The Perseval probe, launched in 2021 by the Meridian Space Agency, reached the asteroid Dakar-7 in September after a three-year journey of 1.4 billion kilometers. The asteroid, a dark, rocky body about 480 meters wide, has a surface covered with boulders, and images show that it spins once every 5.2 hours. Over the next 18 months the probe will map the surface in detail, then lower itself briefly to collect about 100 grams of material using a robotic arm. The sample will return to Earth in a capsule in 2030. Scientists hope the dust will reveal clues about the early solar system, because asteroids like Dakar-7 are leftovers from the era when the planets formed 4.5 billion years ago.
target_summary: The Perseval probe reached asteroid Dakar-7 to collect a sample.

source: A study following 4,600 children in the district of Alder Valley compared students in bilingual programs, which taught half of the school day in Spanish and half in English, with students in English-only classrooms. By the end of sixth grade, the bilingual students had caught up with their peers in English reading and had surpassed them in math by an average of 4 points. They also scored higher on tests of attention and problem solving, and their families reported higher satisfaction with the school. The study found that results were strongest for children who entered the program in kindergarten and weakest for those who joined after third grade. Program costs were about 3 percent higher because of extra teacher training, and the district plans to open six more bilingual schools over the next three years.
target_summary: Bilingual programs matched English reading and improved math in Alder Valley.

source: Small claims courts are designed to resolve minor money disputes quickly and cheaply, without the need for a lawyer. In most regions the claim limit is between 5,000 and 15,000 dollars, and the filing fee is usually under 100 dollars. A person who believes that a landlord has wrongfully kept a deposit, or that a contractor has not completed paid work, can file a claim at the local court and pay to have the other party formally notified. Hearings are informal and typically last under an hour, with each side presenting documents such as receipts, messages, and photographs. Judges may decide on the same day or send a written decision within a few weeks. Winning does not guarantee payment, however, and a claimant may need further steps to collect the money.
target_summary: Small claims courts resolve minor money disputes cheaply without lawyers.

source: A vertical farm in a converted warehouse in Tallow Point now produces 900 kilograms of lettuce, basil, and kale every day, using stacked trays under LED lights and a closed system that recycles water. The operators say the system uses about 95 percent less water than a conventional field and requires no pesticides, since the indoor environment is sealed. Because the farm is only eight kilometers from the city's supermarkets, produce reaches shelves within a day of harvest. The main drawback is energy: lighting and climate control make up nearly 40 percent of operating costs, and the 11 million dollar facility did not turn a profit until its third year. The company is now negotiating a contract for renewable electricity and hopes to open a second site next spring.
target_summary: Tallow Point's vertical farm grows 900 kilograms of greens daily.

Trains reach a top speed of 300 kilometers per hour and run every 20 minutes during the day. Supporters point to benefits such as reduced road traffic and a 12 percent drop in flights between the two cities, since airlines have cut schedules on the route.
