source: The Mural Mile project in the town of Fenwick has transformed 38 blank walls into large paintings, drawing visitors to a neighborhood that was once known for empty storefronts. Launched in 2019 by a local arts nonprofit, the project invites artists from the region to submit designs, and a panel of residents selects winners, who receive 2,500 dollars each. Surveys of nearby businesses found that foot traffic increased by 24 percent between 2019 and 2023, and six new cafes and shops have opened on the main street. Some longtime residents worry that rising popularity could push up rents, and organizers say they will encourage property owners to offer stable leases. A guided walking tour of the murals runs every Saturday and costs 10 dollars, with proceeds funding new walls.
target_summary: Fenwick's Mural Mile revived a neighborhood with 38 murals.

source: Installing solar panels on a house costs roughly 12,000 dollars for a typical 5-kilowatt system after incentives, and it can provide most of a household's electricity during sunny months. The payback period, which is the time needed for electricity savings to equal the installation cost, depends on sunshine, local electricity prices, and the rules for selling surplus power back to the grid. In a sunny region with expensive electricity, payback may take six to eight years, while in a cloudy region with cheap power it can exceed fifteen. Panels usually carry a 25-year performance warranty and slowly lose about half a percent of their output each year. Homeowners are advised to obtain at least three quotes, check that their roof is in good condition, and consider adding a battery only if outages are frequent.
target_summary: Home solar typically pays back in six to fifteen years.

source: Average attendance in the Premier Women's Football League rose to 8,450 per match this season, up from 5,200 two seasons ago, and the final drew a sellout crowd of 41,000 people. The league credits better scheduling, which moved most games to Sunday afternoons, and television coverage that reaches 3.2 million viewers per week. Sponsorship income has tripled to 24 million dollars since 2021, allowing clubs to raise the minimum salary from 18,000 to 45,000 dollars. Despite this progress, players' representatives say that pay remains far below that of male players, and that several clubs still lack year-round access to training grounds. The league has announced that it will expand from 12 to 14 teams in 2026, with new franchises in two mid-sized cities.
target_summary: Women's league attendance rose to 8,450 per match as sponsorship tripled.

source: Every autumn, millions of monarch butterflies in eastern North America fly up to 4,000 kilometers to overwintering sites in the mountain forests of central Mexico. No single butterfly makes the whole round trip. The generation that migrates south lives for up to eight months, while the butterflies that travel north in spring live only a few weeks, and it takes three or four generations to complete the journey back to Canada. Scientists believe the insects navigate using the position of the sun and an internal magnetic compass. Their numbers have fallen sharply since the 1990s, mostly because of the loss of milkweed, the only plant on which monarch caterpillars feed, and because of logging in their winter forests. Conservation groups encourage people to plant native milkweed in gardens and along roadsides.
target_summary: Monarch butterflies migrate thousands of kilometers over several generations.

source: Golden Crust Bakeries, a family business that began as a single shop in 2012, will open 25 franchise locations in the next two years, bringing its total to 40. Founder Elena Ruiz said that demand from franchise applicants, who number more than 300, prompted the move, but that she will accept only owners who complete a six-month training program in the company's central kitchen. Franchisees will pay a fee of 45,000 dollars plus 6 percent of monthly revenue, and the company estimates that a new shop needs about 280,000 dollars to start. To keep quality consistent, dough will be prepared at two regional facilities and delivered daily. Some analysts warn that rapid expansion has damaged other bakery chains, but Ruiz said that growth will be paced to protect the brand.
target_summary: Golden Crust Bakeries will open 25 franchises, reaching 40 locations.

source: Security experts consistently recommend that people use a password manager, a program that creates and stores a different strong password for every account so that users only need to remember one master password. Reusing the same password on several sites is dangerous, because when one site is breached, attackers try the stolen password on others. A 2023 study found that 65 percent of internet users reuse passwords, and that the average person has more than 80 online accounts. Good password managers encrypt the data on the user's device, meaning even the company cannot read it, and they can warn users when a stored password has appeared in a known breach. Experts advise choosing a long master password of at least 16 characters and enabling two-factor authentication on the manager itself.
target_summary: Password managers store unique strong passwords, preventing damage from password reuse.

source: The printing press with movable metal type, developed by Johannes Gutenberg in Mainz around 1450, made it possible to produce books far faster and more cheaply than copying them by hand. A scribe might spend a year copying one Bible, while a print shop could make hundreds of copies in a similar time. The technology spread quickly: by 1500, presses were operating in more than 250 European towns, and an estimated 20 million volumes had been printed. Cheaper books increased literacy, helped scientific findings to circulate widely, and allowed religious ideas to spread rapidly, contributing to the Protestant Reformation. Printing also standardized spelling and grammar in many languages, since printers needed consistent forms to sell books to readers across wide regions.
target_summary: Gutenberg's movable-type press made books cheaper and spread ideas.

source: A survey of 3,500 employees in 120 companies found that 41 percent reported symptoms of burnout, such as exhaustion, cynicism about their jobs, and reduced effectiveness. The highest rates appeared among workers who regularly put in more than 50 hours per week and those who said they had little control over their schedules. Employees whose managers held regular one-on-one conversations and who felt that their workload was fair were half as likely to report burnout. The survey also found that the problem is costly: burned-out workers were 2.6 times more likely to be actively looking for a new job. The report recommends that employers set realistic deadlines, allow flexible schedules, and train managers to recognize early warning signs instead of relying on wellness programs alone.
target_summary: Burnout affects 41 percent of employees, linked to overwork and low control.

source: Two years after the city of Lowell introduced a charge of 10 cents on single-use plastic bags, the number of bags given out by large retailers has fallen by 72 percent, according to a report from the environment department. Litter surveys along rivers and roads found 38 percent fewer plastic bags, and the program has raised 3.4 million dollars, which is spent on recycling education and tree planting. However, the report also noted that sales of thicker reusable plastic bags increased, and that some shoppers simply bought more of them without reusing them. To address this problem, the city is considering raising the minimum thickness and the price of reusable bags. Retailers said that checkout times have not changed and that most customers now bring their own bags.
target_summary: Lowell's 10-cent bag charge cut plastic bag use 72 percent.

source: The Sahara is the largest hot desert in the world, covering about 9 million square kilometers, an area comparable to the United States. Contrary to popular belief, only about a quarter of it is covered by sand dunes, while the rest consists of rocky plateaus, gravel plains, and dry valleys. Temperatures can exceed 50 degrees Celsius during the day and fall near freezing at night. Rainfall is extremely rare, with some areas receiving less than 25 millimeters per year. Yet the desert was green about 10,000 years ago, when a wetter climate supported lakes, grasslands, and herds of animals, as shown by rock paintings found in Algeria and Libya. Today, around two and a half million people live in the Sahara, many of them around scattered oases.
target_summary: The Sahara is the largest hot desert, mostly rock rather than sand.

source: A telemedicine program connecting 18 rural clinics in the Highmoor region with specialists in the city has cut average waiting time for a specialist appointment from 47 days to 9. Patients visit their local clinic, where a nurse helps them connect by video to a doctor and can use digital tools such as a stethoscope that transmits heart sounds. In its first two years, the program handled 12,000 consultations and saved patients an estimated 1.1 million kilometers of travel. Satisfaction surveys show that 91 percent of patients would use the service again. The main obstacles have been unreliable internet connections in two villages and doctors' concerns about missing physical signs. The regional health department intends to extend the program to dermatology and mental health services next year.
target_summary: Telemedicine cut rural specialist waits from 47 to 9 days.

source: Opportunity cost is a basic idea in economics: the true cost of any choice is the value of the next best alternative that you give up. Suppose a student has a free Saturday and can either work a shift that pays 90 dollars or attend a friend's wedding. If she chooses the wedding, her cost is not only the price of the gift and travel but also the 90 dollars she did not earn. Businesses use the concept when deciding how to use limited resources: a farmer who plants wheat on a field cannot plant corn on it, so the profit from corn is part of the cost of growing wheat. Recognizing opportunity cost helps people compare options fairly, since the cheapest-looking choice is not always the best.
target_summary: Opportunity cost is the value of the best alternative forgone.

source: Vaccines work by teaching the immune system to recognize a germ without causing the disease. A vaccine contains a harmless piece or weakened form of a virus or bacterium, or instructions that make cells produce one of its proteins. The immune system responds by producing antibodies and by creating memory cells that can remain in the body for years. If the vaccinated person later meets the real germ, those memory cells recognize it quickly and launch a strong defense before the illness can take hold. Some vaccines, such as those for tetanus, require booster doses because protection fades over time. When enough people in a community are immune, the germ has trouble spreading, which protects infants and people who cannot be vaccinated for medical reasons.
target_summary: Vaccines train the immune system to recognize germs safely.

source: The city of Wexford has replaced 24,000 sodium street lamps with LED lights over three years, cutting its public lighting electricity use by 58 percent. The 14 million dollar project is expected to pay for itself in seven years through lower energy and maintenance bills, since LED lamps last about 15 years, compared with four years for the old ones. The new lights can be dimmed late at night and are controlled remotely, which allowed the city to reduce brightness by 30 percent between midnight and 5 a.m. on quiet streets. source: Restaurants throw away a large share of the food they buy, with studies estimating that between 4 and 10 percent of purchased food becomes waste before it reaches a customer's plate. A pilot program in 60 restaurants in the city of Merrow asked kitchens to weigh and record discarded food for three months using a simple scale and tablet. By identifying patterns, such as unpopular side dishes and oversized portions, participants reduced waste by 26 percent and saved an average of 7,300 dollars each. Chefs changed menus, trained staff to trim vegetables more carefully, and donated surplus meals to a local shelter. Program leaders said that measuring waste was the most important step, because most managers had underestimated how much was thrown away, and they plan to enroll 200 more restaurants next year.
target_summary: A pilot cut restaurant food waste by 26 percent through measurement.

source: Independent bookstores in the country increased in number from 1,650 in 2015 to 2,570 last year, reversing a long decline caused by online retailers and large chains. Store owners say that customers value personal recommendations and events such as author readings, book clubs, and children's story hours. Many shops have also diversified, adding cafes, gift sections, and online ordering for local delivery. The Harbor Page, a bookstore in Dunmore, expanded last year by moving into a larger space and now employs 14 people, twice as many as in 2019. Still, margins are slim, and owners often depend on rent stability. A trade association survey found that 58 percent of stores reported higher sales than the year before, but that one in five owners worried about whether they could afford rising rents.
target_summary: Independent bookstores rebounded to 2,570 stores through events and diversification.

source: The Lyrid meteor shower peaks in the night of 22 April, when observers in the Northern Hemisphere can expect to see about 15 to 20 meteors per hour under dark skies. The meteors come from dust left by the comet Thatcher and appear to radiate from the constellation Lyra, which rises in the northeast after nightfall. This year the moon is a thin crescent that sets early, so the sky will be dark after midnight, giving ideal viewing conditions. Experts advise finding a spot away from city lights, lying back with a clear view of the sky, and allowing 20 to 30 minutes for eyes to adjust to the dark. No telescope or binoculars are needed, since they narrow the field of view, and the best viewing time is the hours before dawn.
target_summary: The Lyrid meteor shower peaks on the night of 22 April.

source: A construction company in the town of Elmstead has built a two-bedroom house in 19 days using a giant 3D printer that deposits layers of concrete to form the walls. The 90-square-meter home cost 138,000 dollars, about 25 percent less than a similar house built with conventional methods, mainly because the printing process requires fewer workers and produces little waste. After the printer finished the walls, crews added the roof, windows, plumbing, and wiring by hand. Engineers tested the structure and found that it meets local standards for earthquake resistance. The company says that it has received orders for 40 more houses, including a development of affordable homes for seniors, but it admits that finding trained operators and obtaining building permits remain challenges, because many local authorities have no rules for printed buildings.
target_summary: Elmstead built a 3D-printed concrete house in 19 days.

source: The remote village of Santa Lucia, home to 1,200 people in the mountains of Peru, gained reliable internet access in March through a community-owned network of solar-powered antennas and a satellite link. Residents pay 8 dollars per month, about one third of the price offered by commercial providers, and the cooperative that runs the network reinvests profits in maintenance. Teachers say that students can now use online learning materials, and local farmers use mobile apps to check market prices for coffee before selling. Within six months, 70 percent of households had subscribed. The network was built with 95,000 dollars from a development fund and training for ten villagers as technicians. Planners are working to replicate the model in 15 other villages in the region.
target_summary: Santa Lucia gained community-owned internet, costing 8 dollars monthly.

source: Airlines worldwide mishandled about 7.6 bags per 1,000 passengers last year, a rate that has improved since 2007, when the figure was more than double. Most problems occur when passengers change planes, since bags must be moved between flights in a short time. Of the mishandled bags, about 80 percent are delayed and eventually delivered, 15 percent are damaged or stolen, and 5 percent are never found. Travelers can reduce the risk by allowing enough time between connecting flights, placing contact details inside the bag as well as outside, and taking photographs of luggage before checking it. Putting a small tracking tag in a suitcase can also help locate it quickly. Passengers should report missing baggage at the airport before leaving, as claims made later are often denied.
target_summary: Bag mishandling has declined to 7.6 per 1,000 passengers.

source: Mangrove forests, which grow in salty coastal water in tropical regions, protect shorelines by absorbing wave energy, store up to four times more carbon per hectare than most land forests, and shelter young fish. Yet about a third of the world's mangroves have been lost since 1980, mostly to shrimp farms and coastal development. In the Bay of Tamarin, villagers have replanted 1,100 hectares of mangroves since 2012 with support from a conservation charity. Fish catches in nearby waters have risen by 30 percent, and when a cyclone struck in 2022, villages behind the restored forest suffered far less damage than those without it. Replanting survives best when species are matched to local conditions, and the project's survival rate of 68 percent is much higher than the 20 percent typical of earlier efforts.
target_summary: Replanted Tamarin mangroves raised fish catches and protected villages from a cyclone.

source: The province of Westmark is short of about 2,300 teachers, with the greatest gaps in mathematics, science, and rural schools. To fill the need, the education ministry has launched a program that offers professionals changing careers a one-year paid training course followed by a three-year commitment to teach in a high-need school. Participants receive a salary of 32,000 dollars during training, and a 10,000 dollar bonus after completing their second year of teaching. In its first cohort, 410 people enrolled, among them engineers, nurses, and accountants, and 86 percent finished the course. Teachers' unions welcomed the effort but said that improving pay and workloads is also necessary to keep new teachers, noting that one in four leaves the profession within five years.
target_summary: Westmark's career-changer program trains teachers to fill 2,300 shortages.

source: Health agencies generally suggest that adults drink about 2.7 liters of total fluid per day for women and 3.7 liters for men, but this figure includes water from food and other drinks, which supplies roughly 20 percent. The actual amount a person needs varies with body size, climate, and physical activity. Thirst is usually a reliable guide for healthy people, and pale yellow urine is a simple sign of adequate hydration. Signs of dehydration include dark urine, headaches, dizziness, and fatigue, and older adults are at higher risk because their sense of thirst weakens with age. Drinking excessive amounts of water in a short time can also be dangerous, since it dilutes the sodium level in the blood, a condition that most often affects endurance athletes.
target_summary: Adults need roughly 2.7 to 3.7 liters of fluid daily.

source: A survey of 1,200 maintainers of open-source software projects found that 60 percent work without any payment, even though their libraries are used by thousands of companies. Many said they feel overwhelmed by user demands: one in three had considered quitting in the past year, and 44 percent reported receiving abusive messages. The problem became widely discussed after a flaw in a small logging library, maintained by volunteers, exposed millions of servers in 2021. In response, several technology companies and foundations created funds, and a European technology fund has granted 23 million euros to critical projects. The authors of the survey recommend that companies that rely on open-source tools contribute money or developer time, and that projects clearly define the level of support they are willing to offer.
target_summary: Most open-source maintainers work unpaid and feel overwhelmed.

source: The Silk Road was not a single road but a network of overland and sea routes that connected China with the Mediterranean from about the second century BCE until the fifteenth century CE. Merchants rarely traveled the entire distance; instead, goods passed through many hands, with traders at oases and cities such as Samarkand and Kashgar buying and selling along the way. Silk was the most famous product, but caravans also carried spices, glassware, precious stones, paper, and horses. The routes spread more than goods: Buddhism traveled from India into China along them, and technologies such as papermaking reached the Islamic world and later Europe. The network declined when Ottoman control of key territories made overland trade costly and when European sailors found sea routes to Asia.
target_summary: The Silk Road was a trade network connecting China and the Mediterranean.

source: A heat wave that began on 28 June has pushed temperatures above 40 degrees Celsius in much of the Kellen Basin for nine consecutive days, breaking a record set in 1998. Hospitals have reported a 35 percent rise in emergency visits for heat-related illness, with the elderly and outdoor workers most affected. Authorities opened 85 cooling centers and urged residents to drink water, avoid strenuous activity between noon and 4 p.m., and check on elderly neighbors. Electricity demand also reached an all-time high of 14.2 gigawatts, forcing utilities to ask households to reduce use of air conditioners during the evening. Meteorologists say a stalled high-pressure system is responsible, and they forecast that temperatures will drop by about six degrees at the end of the week.
target_summary: A record heat wave hit Kellen Basin, raising heat-related hospital visits.

Authorities opened 85 cooling centers and urged residents to drink water, avoid strenuous activity between noon and 4 p.m., and check on elderly neighbors. Electricity demand also reached an all-time high of 14.2 gigawatts, forcing utilities to ask households to reduce use of air conditioners during the evening. Meteorologists say a stalled high-pressure system is responsible, and they forecast that temperatures will drop by about six degrees at the end of the week.
target_summary: A heat wave above 40 degrees Celsius for nine days broke Kellen Basin's record, raising heat-related emergency visits 35 percent and electricity demand.

source: Tides are the regular rise and fall of sea level caused mainly by the moon's gravity. The moon pulls on the ocean facing it, creating a bulge of water, and a second bulge forms on the opposite side of Earth because of the way the planet and moon orbit each other. As the Earth rotates, a given coast passes through both bulges, so most places experience two high tides and two low tides each day, roughly 12 hours and 25 minutes apart. The sun also affects tides: when the sun, moon, and Earth line up at new and full moon, the combined pull produces stronger spring tides, while at the quarter moons the pulls partly cancel, creating weaker neap tides. The Bay of Fundy in Canada has the largest tidal range, reaching about 16 meters.
target_summary: Tides come mainly from the moon's gravity, producing two highs daily.

source: An index fund is an investment fund that aims to match the performance of a market index, such as a list of the 500 largest companies in a country, instead of trying to beat it. Because the fund simply buys the stocks in the index, it needs little research or trading, and its annual fees are very low, often 0.1 percent of the invested amount, compared with about 1 percent for actively managed funds. Over long periods, most active managers fail to outperform the market after fees, which is the main reason index funds have become popular. Investors should note that an index fund will rise and fall with the market, so it carries risk, and it is generally suited to long-term goals. Choosing a broad fund spreads money across hundreds of companies.
target_summary: Index funds track market indexes with low fees.

source: Copyright, trademarks, and patents protect different kinds of creations, and people often confuse them. Copyright covers original works such as books, songs, photographs, and software code, and it arises automatically when the work is created, generally lasting for the author's life plus 70 years in many countries. A trademark protects a name, logo, or slogan that identifies a business's products, and it can last indefinitely as long as it is used and renewed, though it usually must be registered to be enforced strongly. A patent protects a new invention, such as a machine or process, for about 20 years in exchange for a public description of how it works. A bakery's recipe book is covered by copyright, its shop logo by trademark, and a new oven mechanism it invented by a patent.
target_summary: Copyright, trademarks, and patents protect different kinds of creations.

source: The Calbrook Dam, completed in 1962, holds back a reservoir of 1.2 billion cubic meters of water that supplies drinking water to 900,000 people and generates 180 megawatts of electricity. After heavy rains in 2019 pushed the water level within one meter of the crest, inspectors concluded that the dam's spillway, the channel that releases excess water, was too small for the largest predicted floods. A 340 million dollar project now under construction will widen the spillway and add a second channel, increasing its capacity by 60 percent. Work is being done in stages so that the reservoir can stay in service, and it is scheduled to finish in 2027. In the meantime, operators have lowered the maximum water level by two meters during the wet season as a precaution.
target_summary: Calbrook Dam's spillway is being enlarged for larger floods.

source: Kimchi, the Korean dish of fermented vegetables, is typically made from napa cabbage, radish, garlic, ginger, and chili pepper. The cabbage is first soaked in salt for several hours to draw out water, then rinsed and mixed with a spiced paste before being packed in a jar. During fermentation, lactic acid bacteria that naturally live on the vegetables convert sugars into acid, giving kimchi its tangy flavor and preserving it for months. The process takes one to five days at room temperature, after which the kimchi is stored in a refrigerator, where it continues to ripen slowly. Fermented foods such as kimchi contain live bacteria, and early studies suggest that they may support digestive health, although researchers say more evidence is needed. In Korea, families traditionally prepare large batches in late autumn.
target_summary: Kimchi is fermented vegetables, tangy and preserved by lactic acid bacteria.

source: A study of 1,100 university students found that those who described themselves as frequent procrastinators earned lower grades and reported higher stress at the end of the semester. Surprisingly, the researchers concluded that procrastination is less about poor time management than about managing emotions: students put off tasks that made them feel anxious, bored, or unsure, and the short-term relief encouraged them to repeat the pattern. Students who treated themselves kindly after a delay were less likely to procrastinate on the next assignment than those who criticized themselves harshly. The team suggests breaking tasks into small steps, starting with just ten minutes of work, and removing distractions such as phone notifications. They add that deadlines set by instructors for each stage of a project were more effective than a single final deadline.
target_summary: Procrastination stems from managing emotions rather than poor time management.

source: Vinyl record sales in the country reached 6.1 million units last year, the highest figure since 1988, and for the second year running outsold compact discs. Industry analysts attribute the revival to younger listeners, who value the large cover art, the ritual of placing a record on a turntable, and the sense of owning something physical. About half of buyers are under 35, and many do not own a record player at all, using the albums as collectibles. The revival has created problems for the industry: only about 40 pressing plants remain worldwide, so new records can take up to nine months to produce. Prices have also risen, with a new album now costing around 30 dollars on average. Several labels are investing in new factories to meet demand.
target_summary: Vinyl sales hit 6.1 million, driven by younger collectors.

source: Online marketplace ThriftLoop reported that the value of goods sold on its platform rose 29 percent to 2.4 billion dollars last year, as shoppers looked for cheaper alternatives to new products. Clothing remained the biggest category, but furniture and electronics grew fastest, up 41 percent. The company, which charges sellers a commission of 10 percent, said that it now has 18 million active buyers, many of them under 30 and motivated partly by environmental concerns. To build trust, ThriftLoop has introduced identity checks for sellers and a guarantee that refunds buyers if an item does not match its description. It faces rising competition from traditional retailers that have launched their own resale programs, and analysts expect the secondhand market to grow twice as fast as the general retail sector over the next five years.
target_summary: ThriftLoop's resale sales rose 29 percent to 2.4 billion dollars.

source: Farmers in the semi-arid Dodoma region of Tanzania are switching from maize to pearl millet, a grain that tolerates drought and poor soils. In the past five years, maize harvests failed in three seasons because of insufficient rain, leaving many families short of food. Pearl millet needs only about a third of the water that maize requires and matures in 75 days, so it can be harvested before the dry season intensifies. Trials by an agricultural research institute showed that improved millet varieties yielded 1.8 tonnes per hectare, compared with 0.6 for maize in a dry year. The grain is also rich in iron and protein. Challenges remain, such as the limited number of mills for processing and the preference of many consumers for maize flour, and the project is therefore promoting recipes and training women's groups.
target_summary: Tanzanian farmers are switching from maize to drought-tolerant pearl millet.

source: A free school lunch program introduced in the district of Marlowe Heights in 2021 has increased the number of students who eat a hot meal at lunchtime from 52 percent to 94 percent. Previously, only children whose families qualified for support were eligible, and many families did not apply because of stigma or paperwork. Teachers report that students are more attentive in the afternoon, and attendance has risen by 1.5 percentage points. The meals, which must include fruit and vegetables and limit sodium, cost the district 3.40 dollars each, and the program is funded by a combination of state grants and a local levy. Some taxpayers argue that wealthy families should pay, but the district says that universal programs avoid stigma and simplify administration.
target_summary: Free school lunches raised hot-meal participation from 52 to 94 percent.

source: Lightning is a huge electrical discharge that occurs when charges build up in a thunderstorm cloud. Ice crystals and water droplets collide inside the cloud, causing the top to become positively charged and the bottom negatively charged. When the difference becomes large enough, electricity breaks through the air as a lightning bolt, which can heat the surrounding air to about 30,000 degrees Celsius, five times hotter than the surface of the sun. The sudden heating makes the air expand explosively, producing the sound of thunder. Because light travels much faster than sound, people can estimate how far away a strike is by counting the seconds between flash and thunder and dividing by three to get kilometers. Safety experts advise going indoors when thunder is heard and waiting 30 minutes after the last rumble.
target_summary: Lightning discharges built-up charge in thunderstorms, and heated air makes thunder.

source: Cedar Ridge National Park introduced a timed-entry permit system in June after visitor numbers rose from 2.1 million in 2015 to 4.6 million last year, causing traffic jams and overflowing parking lots. Visitors now reserve a two-hour entry window online for 2 dollars, and the park caps daily entries at 9,000 vehicles. In the first season, average wait times at the gate fell from 55 minutes to 8, and trail damage reports decreased by 22 percent. Critics said the system makes it hard for spontaneous travelers and local residents to visit, and that it favors people with good internet access. In response, the park has set aside 15 percent of permits for same-day release and exempted people living in neighboring communities. Park officials will review the program after two years.
target_summary: Cedar Ridge introduced timed-entry permits, cutting gate waits from 55 to 8 minutes.

source: The city council of Brookfield has approved a seven-year contract with Greenway Services for waste and recycling collection, worth 96 million dollars. The new agreement replaces the current system, which has been criticized for missed pickups, with a requirement that the company collect 99 percent of scheduled stops on time or pay penalties of up to 50,000 dollars per month. Households will receive three bins, one for general waste, one for recycling, and one for food scraps, which will be collected weekly, while general waste will be collected every two weeks to encourage recycling. Officials estimate that these changes will divert 30 percent more material from landfill. Some residents worry that fortnightly collection will cause odors in summer, and the council has promised to monitor complaints and review the schedule after six months.

The new agreement replaces the current system, which has been criticized for missed pickups, with a requirement that the company collect 99 percent of scheduled stops on time or pay penalties of up to 50,000 dollars per month. Households will receive three bins, one for general waste, one for recycling, and one for food scraps, which will be collected weekly, while general waste will be collected every two weeks to encourage recycling. Officials estimate that these changes will divert 30 percent more material from landfill. Some residents worry that fortnightly collection will cause odors in summer, and the council has promised to monitor complaints and review the schedule after six months.
target_summary: Brookfield approved a 96 million dollar seven-year waste contract requiring 99 percent on-time collection, three bins, and fortnightly general waste pickup to boost recycling.

source: A network of 600 fast chargers along the country's main highways is now complete, allowing electric vehicle drivers to travel between all major cities with a charging stop at least every 80 kilometers. Built by the operator VoltWay over four years at a cost of 310 million dollars, each station has between 6 and 12 chargers that can add around 300 kilometers of range in 20 minutes. Early data show that the average station is used for about four hours per day, and the operator expects to break even in 2028. Drivers have complained about broken chargers, with 9 percent unavailable at any time, and about the lack of a standard payment method. The government has said it will require operators to maintain 97 percent availability and accept ordinary bank cards from next year.
target_summary: VoltWay completed 600 highway fast chargers, but reliability and payment problems persist.

source: The Skerry Point lighthouse, built in 1858 on a rocky island off the northern coast, guided ships for 130 years before it was automated in 1988. Its tower, made of granite blocks and rising 34 meters, once housed three keepers and their families, who took turns tending the oil lamp and a clockwork mechanism that rotated the lens every 12 minutes. The lens, a complex arrangement of glass prisms, could be seen from 40 kilometers away. In 2004 a local trust took over the station after the government proposed demolition, and it has since restored the buildings and opened them as a museum that receives around 25,000 visitors a year. Visitors can climb the 164 steps to the lantern room, and volunteers run guided tours from April to October.
target_summary: Skerry Point lighthouse, built in 1858, is now a museum.

source: The human gut contains trillions of bacteria, which together weigh about 1.5 kilograms and include hundreds of species. These microbes help digest fibers that the body cannot break down, producing short-chain fatty acids that nourish the cells lining the intestine, and they play a part in training the immune system and producing certain vitamins. A diverse mix of microbes is generally considered a sign of good health, and diet is one of the strongest influences on it. People who eat a wide range of plant foods, such as vegetables, legumes, whole grains, and fruit, tend to have a more diverse community than those who consume mostly processed foods. Antibiotics can temporarily reduce diversity, but the community usually recovers within weeks. Researchers are studying whether altering gut bacteria could treat diseases, though most evidence is still preliminary.
target_summary: Gut microbes aid digestion and immunity, and diverse plant foods support them.

source: A report on 14 coding bootcamps found that 71 percent of graduates found a job in a technology role within six months of finishing the program, and that their median salary rose from 38,000 to 63,000 dollars. Bootcamps typically run for 12 to 24 weeks and cost between 10,000 and 18,000 dollars, far less than a four-year degree. However, outcomes varied widely: graduates from the three best programs had job placement rates above 85 percent, while the weakest had rates of 48 percent. The report also found that students who already had a college degree or prior programming experience were far more likely to find jobs, and that entry-level positions have become more competitive. The authors advise prospective students to ask for audited placement data and to complete projects that they can show to employers.
target_summary: Coding bootcamp graduates often find jobs, but outcomes vary widely.

source: A severe drought has forced authorities in the Isthmus Canal to cut the number of ships allowed to cross each day from 36 to 24, after water levels in the lakes that supply the locks fell to their lowest point in 70 years. Each ship that passes through the canal uses about 200 million liters of fresh water, so reducing traffic is the quickest way to save supply. Shipping companies have faced delays of up to two weeks and have paid premiums of as much as 4 million dollars at auctions to secure slots. Some have chosen to sail around the southern tip of the continent, adding 12 days to the journey. The canal authority is building a new reservoir, due to be ready in 2030, and says that rains expected in November should begin to restore water levels.
target_summary: Drought forced the Isthmus Canal to cut daily crossings from 36 to 24.

source: The Sunrise Community Garden, started in 2016 on an empty lot in the Eastbank neighborhood, has grown into a space with 85 raised beds tended by 140 families. Members pay an annual fee of 25 dollars and volunteer four hours per month to maintain shared areas, such as the compost bins and a small orchard. Gardeners estimate that they grow about 6 tonnes of vegetables each year, and a portion is donated to a nearby food pantry. The garden also hosts free workshops on composting and cooking, which attract around 50 people per session. Organizers say the greatest benefit is social, since many members did not know their neighbors before joining. The lease runs out in 2027, and the group is raising money to buy the land from the city for 180,000 dollars.
target_summary: Sunrise Community Garden hosts 140 families on 85 raised beds.

source: Storm surge, the abnormal rise of seawater pushed ashore by a hurricane's winds, causes more deaths than the winds themselves. A surge of three to five meters can flood coastal neighborhoods within minutes, and it is dangerous because it arrives together with high tide and waves. The Gulf Coast city of Port Merel, which was hit by a surge of 4.2 meters in 2017, has since built a 12-kilometer sea wall and raised 1,800 homes on stilts, at a cost of 410 million dollars. Emergency managers also issue evacuation orders by zone, based on how far water could reach, instead of ordering whole counties to leave. Residents are advised to leave early, since roads can flood hours before the storm arrives, and to bring documents, medicines, and enough water for three days.
target_summary: Storm surge kills more than hurricane winds; evacuate early.

source: Each summer, loggerhead sea turtles crawl onto the beaches of Cape Solano to lay about 110 eggs each in nests dug into the sand. Because artificial lights confuse hatchlings, which normally crawl toward the brighter horizon over the sea, conservationists persuaded 14 coastal hotels to switch to amber lights and to close their curtains at night. Volunteers patrol the beach at dawn, mark every nest, and place wire cages over them to protect eggs from foxes. These measures raised the hatching success from 48 percent to 71 percent over six years, and last season recorded 1,420 nests, the most since counting began in 1998. Scientists caution that only about one in a thousand hatchlings survives to adulthood, so protection of the nesting beaches must be accompanied by action to reduce accidental capture in fishing nets.
target_summary: Hotel lighting changes and nest protection boosted sea turtle hatching success.

source: Archaeologists using laser scanning from aircraft have discovered a network of raised roads hidden beneath the forest of the Yucan lowlands, revealing that the region supported a far larger population than previously believed. The scans, which covered 2,100 square kilometers, show 17 ancient towns connected by straight causeways up to 22 meters wide and a total length of about 240 kilometers. The roads, built around 700 CE, linked farming areas to a central market city where goods such as cacao, salt, and obsidian were exchanged. Dr. Tomas Herrera, who led the survey, said that the technology allowed his team to map in two weeks what would have taken decades on foot. Excavations will start next year at three sites, and the government has promised to protect the area from illegal logging.
target_summary: Laser scans revealed an ancient road network beneath Yucan forest.

source: A laboratory study of 120 adults found that a nap of 20 minutes improved alertness and reaction time for up to three hours, while a nap of 60 minutes improved memory for facts but left participants groggy for about half an hour afterward. This groggy feeling, called sleep inertia, occurs when a person wakes from deep sleep, which usually begins after 30 minutes. Participants who napped for 20 minutes between 1 and 3 p.m. reported better mood and made 34 percent fewer errors on an attention task than those who did not nap. Naps late in the afternoon, however, reduced the amount of sleep people got at night by an average of 25 minutes. The researchers suggest that people who need a boost should nap early in the afternoon and set an alarm.
target_summary: Twenty-minute naps improve alertness; sixty-minute naps help memory but cause grogginess.

source: A ransomware attack on the Beacon Regional Medical Center on 4 February locked the hospital's computer systems, forcing staff to use paper records for 11 days and to divert ambulances to other hospitals for the first three. Elective surgeries were postponed, and about 600 appointments were rescheduled. The attackers demanded 3.5 million dollars in cryptocurrency, but hospital officials said they refused to pay and restored the systems from backups with the help of outside security experts. Investigators believe that the attackers entered through a phishing email opened by an employee in the billing department. The hospital has since introduced mandatory security training, two-step login for all staff, and a separate network for medical devices. Federal authorities are investigating, and the hospital says it has no evidence that patient data was stolen.
target_summary: Ransomware forced Beacon hospital onto paper records for 11 days.

source: The University of Ardmore announced that from next year all research papers written by its staff must be made freely available online within 12 months of publication. Currently the university pays about 9 million dollars each year in subscriptions to academic journals, and prices have risen by an average of 6 percent annually for a decade. Librarians say that the new policy will make research accessible to people outside universities, including patients, teachers, and small businesses, and will give the institution more bargaining power with publishers. Some journals charge authors fees of 2,000 to 5,000 dollars to publish openly, so the university will set up a fund to cover these costs for early-career researchers. Critics fear that the fees may favor well-funded laboratories, and the university will review the system after three years.
target_summary: Ardmore University will require its research papers to be freely available online.

source: Cover crops are plants such as clover, rye, and vetch that farmers grow between harvests to protect and improve the soil. Their roots hold the soil in place during heavy rain, reducing erosion by as much as 60 percent, and legumes like clover take nitrogen from the air and add it to the soil, lowering fertilizer needs. In a ten-year trial on 40 farms in the Marren Valley, fields with cover crops contained 18 percent more organic matter and held more water during dry spells than fields left bare. Corn yields were about 4 percent higher in the sixth year of the trial. Farmers do face costs: seed and planting add roughly 45 dollars per hectare, and cover crops must be terminated before the main crop is planted, which requires careful timing.

source: A disused textile mill in the city of Halbrook, built in 1896, has been converted into 212 apartments, a market hall, and a small museum of local industry. The 68 million dollar project retained the building's brick walls, cast-iron columns, and tall windows, while adding insulation and a rooftop garden. Developers said that reusing the existing structure produced about 40 percent less embodied carbon than demolishing it and building new, since making concrete and steel is energy intensive. Thirty of the apartments are reserved for residents with moderate incomes, and the market hall hosts 35 small vendors. Some neighbors worried about parking and noise during construction, which lasted three years, but the project has been praised by heritage groups. The city is considering similar reuse plans for two other former factories.
target_summary: Halbrook converted an 1896 textile mill into 212 apartments.

source: A study of 300 university students compared reading comprehension of a 3,000-word article on paper, on a tablet, and on an e-reader with a non-glare screen. Students who read on paper scored 6 percent higher on questions about the order of events and the details of the text, although there was no difference in their understanding of the main ideas. Researchers suggest that the physical feel of paper helps readers build a mental map of where information sits in the text. The effect was smaller for students who regularly read on screens, and it disappeared when readers spent more time on the task. The authors conclude that digital reading is adequate for most purposes, but that people who need to remember specific details, such as when studying for exams, may benefit from printed materials.
target_summary: Paper readers recalled text details slightly better than screen readers.

source: A microloan program in the Rift Valley district of Kenya has lent an average of 280 dollars to 9,500 women to start or expand small businesses such as tailoring, poultry keeping, and selling vegetables. Borrowers form groups of five who guarantee one another's loans and meet weekly to make repayments, which has resulted in a repayment rate of 97 percent. A three-year evaluation found that the women's household income rose by 23 percent on average, and that they were more likely to pay school fees for their children. However, the study also found that very small loans do not help everyone, as borrowers who already had experience in trading benefited most, while some of the poorest struggled with the weekly payments. The program has now added savings accounts and business training to better support new entrepreneurs.
target_summary: Kenyan microloans raised women borrowers' household income 23 percent.

source: The city of La Serena Alta opened a 4.6-kilometer cable car in March that links a hillside district of 80,000 people to the city center in 17 minutes, replacing a bus journey that took more than an hour on steep, congested roads. The system has five stations and cabins that carry ten passengers each, and it can move up to 3,000 people per hour in each direction. Fares are the same as the bus, 1.20 dollars, and the line carried 6,400 passengers per day in its first month. Built for 52 million dollars, the cable car cost less than a quarter of what a metro line would have and took 14 months to complete. Residents say that it has cut travel times, but some complain that cabins are overcrowded at 8 a.m., and the operator plans to add 30 more cabins.
target_summary: La Serena Alta's cable car cut a hillside commute to 17 minutes.

source: Peatlands cover only three percent of the Earth's land surface but store about twice as much carbon as all the world's forests combined. When they are drained for farming or fuel, the peat dries out and releases carbon dioxide, and drained peatlands are estimated to account for about four percent of global emissions. In the Moorvale region of Scotland, a project begun in 2018 has blocked 2,400 drainage ditches and replanted native bog mosses on 3,800 hectares. Measurements show that the water table has risen by an average of 15 centimeters and that the restored areas have started absorbing carbon again. Birds such as curlews and golden plovers have also returned. The work costs about 1,500 dollars per hectare, and the land managers are being paid by companies that purchase carbon credits to offset their emissions.
target_summary: Peatlands store huge carbon; restoring drained peat reduces emissions.

source: A youth soccer club in the town of Redhill has trained 60 volunteer parents as coaches through a free course covering safety, basic skills, and how to give constructive feedback. Before the program, one in three coaches had no formal training, and the club lost about a quarter of its players aged 10 to 14 each year, mostly because children felt discouraged. After two years, player retention rose from 74 to 89 percent, and the number of injuries reported fell by 30 percent. The course takes eight hours over two weekends and is taught by licensed coaches from the regional federation. Parents said that they had learned to focus on development instead of winning, and the club has expanded the program to include girls' teams, which have grown from two to seven.
target_summary: Redhill's coach training raised youth soccer retention from 74 to 89 percent.

source: Olive harvest in the Mediterranean usually runs from October to January, and the timing affects the quality of the oil. Olives picked early, while still green, yield less oil but give a peppery, fresh flavor and contain more of the antioxidants known as polyphenols, whereas fully ripe black olives produce more oil with a milder taste. To make extra virgin oil, producers must crush the olives within about 24 hours of picking and press them mechanically without heat or chemicals, and the oil must pass chemical and taste tests, including having acidity below 0.8 percent. A tree produces on average 15 to 20 kilograms of olives per year, which gives roughly three liters of oil. Oil should be kept in a cool, dark place and used within 18 months.
target_summary: Early-picked olives give peppery, polyphenol-rich oil; ripe ones yield more.

source: The bystander effect is the finding that people are less likely to help someone in need when other people are present. In a classic 1968 experiment, participants who believed they were alone with a person suffering a seizure over an intercom reported it 85 percent of the time within a few minutes, but when they thought four other people were listening, only 31 percent did so. Psychologists explain the result by diffusion of responsibility, since each person assumes someone else will act, and by social cues, since people look to others for signs of whether a situation is truly an emergency. Later research shows that the effect weakens if the situation is clearly dangerous or if bystanders know one another. Training courses teach people to point to a specific person and ask directly for help.
target_summary: People help less when others are present, called the bystander effect.

source: The town of Hveralund has begun supplying heat to 2,300 homes through a district network fed by two geothermal wells drilled 2.8 kilometers deep, where water reaches 92 degrees Celsius. The hot water is pumped to a central station, passes through heat exchangers, and flows through insulated pipes to buildings, replacing individual gas boilers. The 74 million dollar project, completed in 2023, is expected to cut the town's carbon emissions by 11,000 tonnes per year and reduce the average household heating bill by 22 percent. Drilling took longer than planned because the first well was unproductive, which added 9 million dollars to the cost. Engineers say that the underground reservoir can supply heat for at least 50 years. The council is now exploring whether neighboring villages could join the network.
target_summary: Hveralund's geothermal network heats 2,300 homes, cutting emissions.

source: Right-to-repair laws require manufacturers to make spare parts, tools, and repair manuals available to customers and independent repair shops. Supporters say that such rules reduce electronic waste, which reached 62 million tonnes worldwide in 2022, and save consumers money, since a battery replacement at an independent shop often costs half as much as the manufacturer's service. The law passed in the state of Marlow in January covers smartphones, laptops, and household appliances sold after July, and it requires parts to be offered for seven years. Manufacturers have argued that opening repairs to outsiders may compromise safety and security, and that it could expose their intellectual property. The law includes an exemption for products such as medical devices, and the attorney general will begin enforcing penalties of up to 5,000 dollars per violation next year.
target_summary: Right-to-repair laws make manufacturers supply parts, tools, and manuals.

source: An airplane stays in the air because its wings generate lift, an upward force created when air flows over and under them. A wing is shaped and tilted so that it pushes air downward as it moves forward; by Newton's third law, the air pushes the wing upward. At the same time, air flowing over the curved top surface moves faster and has lower pressure than air beneath, and the pressure difference also contributes to lift. The amount of lift depends on the speed of the aircraft, the size of the wings, and the angle at which they meet the air, which pilots can increase to climb. If the angle becomes too steep, however, the airflow separates from the wing and lift falls suddenly, a condition called a stall. Pilots avoid this by keeping enough speed and lowering the nose.
target_summary: Wings create lift by deflecting air downward and lowering pressure above.

source: Radio dramas, once thought to be a relic of the 1940s, are experiencing a revival in the form of podcasts, with more than 3,000 fiction titles now available in English. Production costs are low compared with television, since a series requires only actors, a sound designer, and a writer, and listeners can enjoy them while commuting or exercising. A survey by the Audio Storytelling Association found that 28 percent of podcast listeners tried a fiction series last year, up from 14 percent in 2019. The most successful series have been mysteries and science fiction, and several have been sold to television studios. Producers say the challenge is making money, since only about one in ten series earns enough from sponsors and subscriptions to pay its cast, and many rely on volunteer work.
target_summary: Radio dramas are reviving as podcasts, though few earn enough.

source: The Hollin Construction Training Board reported that 1,850 people began apprenticeships in building trades such as electrical work, plumbing, and carpentry this year, 22 percent more than last year. Apprentices spend four days a week working on sites for a salary that starts at 18 dollars per hour and rises as they gain skills, and one day in classroom training. source: Astronomers using the Corvus Space Telescope have discovered a rocky planet about 1.1 times the size of Earth orbiting a small red star 38 light-years away. The planet, designated Corvus-4b, circles its star every 12 days at a distance where temperatures could allow liquid water on the surface, although the star's frequent flares may strip away the atmosphere. The finding was made by measuring tiny dips in the star's brightness as the planet passed in front of it. Researchers have booked observing time on a larger telescope next year to look for gases such as water vapor and carbon dioxide in the planet's atmosphere. Lead scientist Dr. Anika Rao cautioned that the planet's habitability is uncertain, and that the discovery should be seen as a promising target, not evidence of life.
target_summary: Astronomers found a possibly habitable Earth-sized planet 38 light-years away.

source: New guidelines from the Pediatric Health Council recommend that children under two avoid screens except for video calls, and that children aged two to five be limited to one hour of high-quality programming a day with a parent. For older children, the council stopped setting a single hour limit and instead advises families to ensure that screen use does not replace sleep, physical activity, homework, or time with family. A review of 80 studies found that heavy use of more than four hours daily was linked to poorer sleep and lower attention, but the strongest effects were seen when devices were used in bedrooms at night. The guidelines suggest keeping phones out of bedrooms, turning off screens an hour before bed, and creating family media plans that define when and where devices may be used.
target_summary: New guidelines limit toddlers' screens and stress protecting sleep and activity.

source: Cocoa farmers in West Africa typically earn less than two dollars a day, and the fair-trade certification system aims to improve that by guaranteeing a minimum price and an additional premium for community projects. For cocoa, the minimum price is 2,400 dollars per tonne, and the premium of 240 dollars per tonne is used by farmer cooperatives to build schools, wells, and clinics. A study of 60 cooperatives in Ghana found that certified farmers earned about 12 percent more than non-certified neighbors, but that most of the benefit went to the cooperatives and larger farms. Critics also note that only about a third of certified cocoa is actually sold on certified terms, because buyers do not purchase enough. Advocates argue that certification is still one tool among many, along with traceability and stronger government rules.
target_summary: Fair-trade cocoa guarantees minimum prices, but benefits are uneven.

source: A survey of noise levels in the city of Ashgrove found that 41 percent of residents live in areas where average nighttime traffic noise exceeds 55 decibels, a level that health agencies warn can harm health. Chronic noise exposure is associated with higher blood pressure, disturbed sleep, and an increased risk of heart disease, and researchers estimate that noise contributes to about 90 premature deaths per year in the city. The council has therefore lowered speed limits on 60 streets to 30 kilometers per hour, which reduces tire noise by about 3 decibels, and is installing quieter road surfacing on main roads. It also offers subsidies of up to 2,000 dollars for triple-glazed windows in the noisiest homes. A new noise map published online allows residents to check levels at their address.
target_summary: Ashgrove is cutting traffic noise that exposes 41 percent of residents.

source: Soap cleans because its molecules have two different ends: one end is attracted to water, and the other end is attracted to oil and grease. Dirt on skin or clothes is usually held in place by a thin film of oil, which water alone cannot remove. When soap is dissolved in water, the oil-loving ends dig into the grease while the water-loving ends face outward, forming tiny spheres called micelles that trap the oil inside. The micelles are carried away when the skin or fabric is rinsed. Soap is also effective against many viruses, such as coronaviruses, because it can break apart their fatty outer layer. For handwashing, experts recommend scrubbing for at least 20 seconds, making sure to clean between the fingers and under the nails, since friction helps loosen germs from the skin.
target_summary: Soap molecules trap oil in micelles, so water can rinse dirt away.

source: The town of Arden Falls switched on its first electric street lights on 12 October 1893, powered by a small hydroelectric plant built on the river below the falls for 38,000 dollars. The plant, which had two turbines producing a total of 150 kilowatts, initially served 40 street lamps and 130 homes, whose owners paid a flat monthly fee of 1.50 dollars. Newspaper reports of the time described crowds gathering in the main square to watch the lamps ignite at dusk. Within five years the town's two textile mills had replaced steam engines with electric motors, which cut their fuel costs by half and allowed them to expand. The original powerhouse, restored in 1998, now operates as a museum and still generates a small amount of power.
target_summary: Arden Falls lit its first electric street lamps in 1893 using hydropower.

source: Seaweed farming is one of the fastest-growing forms of aquaculture, with global production reaching 35 million tonnes in 2020, more than double the amount two decades earlier. It requires no fresh water, fertilizer, or farmland: ropes are strung in shallow coastal water and seeded with young seaweed, which grows to harvestable size within about three months. Besides food, seaweed is used to make thickening agents for ice cream, animal feed, and fertilizer. Some species absorb nutrients that cause algal blooms and can provide habitat for small fish. In the Kvarn archipelago of Norway, a company has built a 120-hectare farm that yields 1,800 tonnes per year and employs 35 people. Challenges include storms, which can destroy lines, and competition for space with fishing and shipping.
target_summary: Seaweed farming needs no fresh water or farmland and is growing fast.

source: Night train services are returning across Europe as travelers look for alternatives to short flights. The Northern Sleeper, which began running between Stockholm and Hamburg in March, carries 420 passengers per night in seats, couchettes, and private cabins and has been 88 percent full on average. A trip takes 11 hours, and tickets for a seat cost from 59 euros. Operators argue that the trains cut carbon emissions by about 85 percent per passenger compared with flying, and that travelers save the cost of a hotel. However, the services depend on subsidies because the trains are expensive to operate, and many lack modern sleeping cars, since the old ones were retired decades ago. Several countries have ordered new rolling stock, with 110 sleeper cars due for delivery by 2027.
target_summary: Night trains are returning as alternatives to short flights.

source: Conservators in the city of Brescan have used infrared and X-ray imaging to reveal a hidden portrait beneath a seventeenth-century landscape painting attributed to the artist Joris Van Dael. The imaging showed the faint outline of a young woman in a red dress, painted by the same artist and then covered over, perhaps because the original sitter's family declined to buy the portrait. Researchers examined paint samples and found that the pigments in both images are consistent with those available in the 1650s. The landscape, which is owned by the municipal museum, will remain on display, but visitors will be able to view digital reconstructions of the portrait on a screen next to it. Experts say that such discoveries are common, since artists in that period often reused canvases because they were expensive.
target_summary: Imaging revealed a hidden portrait beneath a seventeenth-century Van Dael landscape.

source: Retailers that expanded self-checkout lanes are finding that the technology is more costly than expected. A study of 12 supermarket chains reported that unscanned or wrongly scanned items, whether accidental or deliberate, cause losses of about 4 percent of sales at self-checkout, compared with 1.5 percent at staffed tills. Stores have responded by adding cameras, scales that detect unscanned products, and attendants who monitor four to six lanes at once. Several chains have removed machines from stores where theft was high, and one has limited self-checkout to customers with fewer than ten items. Surveys show that shoppers like the speed of the machines for small purchases, but 47 percent find them frustrating when an item will not scan. Industry analysts predict that stores will use a mix of staffed and automated lanes.
target_summary: Self-checkout losses reach 4 percent of sales, prompting stores to add safeguards.

source: Quantum computers use quantum bits, or qubits, which can exist in a combination of 0 and 1 at the same time, unlike the bits of ordinary computers, which are always one or the other. Because qubits can be linked in a way called entanglement, a quantum computer can in principle explore many possibilities in parallel and solve certain problems much faster than any ordinary machine, such as simulating molecules or breaking some forms of encryption. Building them is difficult, however: qubits are fragile and lose their quantum state if disturbed by heat or vibration, so many machines operate at temperatures near absolute zero. The largest current systems have a few hundred qubits and make frequent errors. Experts expect that useful general-purpose machines remain at least a decade away, and they are developing new forms of encryption to prepare.
target_summary: Quantum computers use qubits that can solve some problems faster.

source: A community choir program for adults over 60 in the town of Wainby has attracted 180 singers since it began in 2021, and a study by the local university suggests it is improving their wellbeing. Participants meet for two hours every Tuesday and perform in public four times a year. In a survey of 90 members, 72 percent said they felt less lonely than before joining, and their scores on a standard measure of mood were 15 percent higher after one year, compared with a similar group that did not sing. Singing together also encourages deep breathing and physical activity. The program costs 18,000 dollars per year, mostly for the conductor's salary and room rental, and is supported by grants and a membership fee of 40 dollars per term. A waiting list of 50 people has led organizers to open a second choir.
target_summary: Wainby's community choir for over-60s reduced loneliness and improved mood.

source: The annual winter bird count at Marlow Wetlands, taken by 85 volunteers on 14 January, recorded 63,400 waterbirds of 71 species, the highest total in 25 years of monitoring. Notable sightings included 412 pintail ducks, a species that has declined across the region, and a pair of rare bitterns. Wetland manager Cora Lindqvist attributed the increase to a restoration project completed in 2022, which re-flooded 300 hectares of former farmland and created shallow pools and islands for nesting. Local counts also show that fish and frog populations have grown. The reserve now receives 30,000 visitors per year, and a new observation hide funded by the local council opens in May. Volunteers will repeat the count in July to monitor breeding birds.
target_summary: Marlow Wetlands recorded 63,400 waterbirds, a 25-year high.

source: Indoor rock climbing has grown from a niche pursuit into a mainstream sport, with the number of climbing gyms in the country increasing from 290 in 2015 to 640 today. The sport entered the Olympic Games in 2021, which brought attention to it, and many gyms attract beginners with introductory classes and low-cost day passes of about 20 dollars. Industry data show that 38 percent of gym visitors are women, a higher share than in most other strength-based sports. Injuries are a concern: a study of 4,000 climbers found that finger and shoulder problems are the most common, and that beginners are especially at risk when they climb too hard too soon. Gyms recommend warming up, resting between sessions, and taking a safety course before climbing with ropes.
target_summary: Climbing gyms more than doubled to 640 as the sport became mainstream.

source: The Midland Blood Service has urgently appealed for donors after stocks of O-negative blood, the type that can be given to almost any patient, fell to under two days' supply in the hospitals it serves. Only about 7 percent of the population has this type, yet it is used in 13 percent of emergency transfusions, when there is no time to test a patient's blood. Donations typically fall in summer holidays and in winter because of illness, and the service needs 1,100 donations every day to meet demand. A donation takes about an hour, including a health check, and the donor can give again after 12 weeks. First-time donors are encouraged to drink plenty of water and eat before donating. Blood has a shelf life of only 35 days, so supplies must be continually replenished.
target_summary: Midland Blood Service urgently seeks donors as O-negative stocks run low.

source: The island nation of Tavelo, with a population of 62,000, earns about 38 percent of its income from tourism, and the sector employs one in four workers. When the pandemic stopped travel in 2020, the economy contracted by 21 percent in a single year, and unemployment tripled. Since then, the government has tried to reduce its dependence on visitors by supporting fishing, coconut processing, and a small digital services industry that now employs 900 people. Tourist arrivals have returned to 94 percent of their earlier level, however, and officials are cautious about limiting the sector, since wages in hotels remain higher than in most other jobs. Economists recommend that the country invest in training and in renewable energy, because imported fuel for electricity costs about 15 percent of national income.
target_summary: Tavelo's tourism-dependent economy is diversifying into fishing and digital services.

source: After a study found that 120 of the 410 public schools in the province of Mirador had not been designed to resist strong earthquakes, the government launched a retrofitting program with a budget of 330 million dollars. Engineers strengthen the buildings by adding steel bracing, reinforcing columns with fiber wraps, and anchoring walls to floors. Work is done during summer vacation to avoid disrupting classes, and a typical school can be upgraded in eight to ten weeks. So far, 46 schools have been completed, and in a magnitude 6.1 earthquake last year, none of the retrofitted buildings suffered structural damage, whereas three older schools were closed for repairs. Officials aim to complete the work by 2029, but the program has been delayed by shortages of skilled workers and rising steel prices.
target_summary: Mirador is retrofitting earthquake-vulnerable schools with a 330 million dollar program.

source: Dairy farmer Anneke Visser installed two robotic milking machines at her farm in the Frisian lowlands, and the cows now decide for themselves when to be milked, visiting the robots an average of 2.9 times a day instead of the two scheduled milkings before. The machines identify each cow by a tag, clean the udder, attach the cups with a robotic arm, and record the quantity and quality of the milk. Visser says that milk production rose 11 percent and that the data help her detect illnesses early. The system cost 280,000 dollars, but she saves about 40 hours of labor per week. Not every farm benefits, however, since the machines work best for herds of 60 to 120 cows and require good internet access, and repairs on weekends can be expensive.
target_summary: Robotic milkers raised one dairy farm's output 11 percent.

source: A test of five widely used translation apps found that they performed well on simple sentences between common languages, such as Spanish to English, with accuracy ratings of over 90 percent from professional reviewers. Their performance dropped to between 55 and 70 percent for idioms, legal texts, and languages with less online data, such as Amharic and Lao. Common mistakes included translating phrases word for word, confusing words with several meanings, and missing differences in politeness. The researchers recommend using the apps for travel and quick understanding but not for medical, legal, or contractual matters, where errors can have serious consequences. They also advise users to write short sentences, avoid slang, and translate the result back into the original language to check that the meaning has not changed.
target_summary: Translation apps excel at simple sentences but struggle with idioms.

source: A sinkhole is a hole that forms in the ground when the surface layer collapses into an empty space underneath. Most occur in regions where the bedrock is limestone or other rock that dissolves slowly in slightly acidic rainwater, creating underground caves. When the roof of a cave becomes too thin to support the soil above, the ground suddenly gives way. Human activity can increase the risk, because pumping out large amounts of groundwater or leaking water pipes can remove the support that keeps the ground intact. In 2023, a sinkhole 20 meters wide and 12 meters deep opened in a car park in the town of Dalsby, swallowing four vehicles, though nobody was injured. Warning signs include cracks in walls, doors that stick, and small depressions in the ground.
target_summary: Sinkholes form when ground collapses into caves dissolved in limestone.

source: Companies are developing machines to collect potato-sized nodules rich in nickel, cobalt, and manganese from the deep ocean floor, 4,000 to 6,000 meters down in a region of the Pacific. Supporters say that these metals are needed for electric vehicle batteries and that mining nodules could cause less harm than digging new mines on land, where it displaces communities and forests. Scientists argue that too little is known about deep-sea ecosystems, which contain thousands of species that are new to science, and that mining would create sediment plumes that could spread over wide areas and take decades to recover. An international authority is negotiating rules, and 32 countries have called for a pause until further studies are done. Several companies have said they will wait for the regulations before starting commercial operations.
target_summary: Deep-sea nodule mining divides supporters seeking battery metals from scientists urging caution.

source: The Wexcombe Historical Society has completed a six-year project to digitize 1.2 million pages of local newspapers published between 1851 and 1975, making them searchable online for free. Volunteers and staff scanned bound volumes of 43 titles, and software converted the images to searchable text, though older pages with faded ink produced error rates of about 12 percent, so a team of 60 volunteers corrected the headlines and the first paragraphs. The project cost 740,000 dollars, funded by a national heritage grant and donations. Since the archive was launched in September, it has received 90,000 visits from 41 countries, many from people researching family history. Teachers have begun using the articles in history lessons, and the society plans to add photographs and advertisements next year.
target_summary: Wexcombe digitized 1.2 million pages of local newspapers for free searching.

source: A study at the University of Tilbrook followed 80 adults aged 55 to 75 who had never played an instrument, half of whom took weekly piano lessons for nine months while the others took part in a general knowledge course. At the end, the pianists performed better on tests of working memory and speed of processing, and brain scans showed greater activity in regions linked to hearing and movement coordination. The improvements were modest, about 8 percent on average, but they persisted for six months after lessons stopped in those who continued to practice. Researchers say the findings support the idea that the adult brain remains adaptable, though they caution that the study was small and cannot show that music lessons prevent age-related decline. Participants also reported enjoying the social aspect of classes.
target_summary: Piano lessons modestly improved older adults' memory and processing speed.

source: The coastal city of Port Verran has approved a 25-year adaptation plan to protect against rising seas, with a budget of 1.4 billion dollars. Sea levels along the coast have risen by 18 centimeters since 1990, and projections suggest another 40 to 80 centimeters by 2100. The plan includes a 9-kilometer sea wall, restored salt marshes that absorb wave energy, elevated roads, and rules that require new buildings in flood zones to be raised by one meter. About 2,600 properties in the lowest areas will be offered voluntary buyouts. Residents have expressed concern about the cost, which will be partly paid by an increase of 0.4 percent in property taxes, and about the loss of ocean views from the wall. Planners say that doing nothing would cost an estimated 3.8 billion dollars in damage by 2060.
target_summary: Port Verran approved a 1.4 billion dollar plan against rising seas.
