source: Dietary fiber, the part of plant foods that the body cannot fully digest, supports digestion and is linked to a lower risk of heart disease and type 2 diabetes. Health authorities recommend that adults eat 25 to 30 grams a day, but most people consume only about 17. Soluble fiber, found in oats, beans, and apples, dissolves in water and helps reduce blood cholesterol, while insoluble fiber, found in whole grains and vegetables, adds bulk and helps food move through the intestines. A review of 185 studies found that people eating the most fiber had a 15 to 30 percent lower risk of dying from heart disease than those eating the least. Nutritionists advise increasing fiber gradually and drinking more water, since a sudden rise can cause bloating and gas.
target_summary: Fiber aids digestion and heart health; most adults eat too little.

source: An after-school tutoring program in the district of Calder Heights has helped 1,200 struggling students improve their reading and math skills, according to an independent evaluation. Students attend three sessions per week of 45 minutes in groups of four with a trained tutor, who follows a structured plan aligned with the school curriculum. After one year, participants gained an average of 1.4 years of progress in reading, compared with 0.9 years for similar students who were not in the program. Absenteeism also declined by 20 percent. The program costs about 1,100 dollars per student, which supporters argue is lower than the cost of repeating a grade. Funding comes from a federal grant that expires next June, and the district is seeking a permanent source of money to maintain the sessions.

source: The Riverside Public Pool, which closed in 2018 after the city declared its heating system unsafe, will reopen on 1 June following a 16 million dollar renovation. The facility has been upgraded with a new 25-meter lap pool, a shallow pool for children, a heat pump system that cuts energy use by 45 percent, and an accessible changing area with a lift for people with limited mobility. Swimming lessons for children will be free for residents for the first year, and entry for adults will cost 5 dollars. Local clubs said that during the closure, swimmers had to travel up to 30 minutes to find a pool, and that the waiting list for lessons exceeded 800 children. The pool will be open from 6 a.m. to 9 p.m. on weekdays and will employ 24 staff.
target_summary: Riverside Public Pool will reopen on 1 June after a renovation.

source: More than 9,000 active satellites now orbit Earth, and the number may exceed 40,000 within a decade as companies launch large constellations for internet service. The risk of collisions is also growing: space agencies track about 36,000 pieces of debris larger than ten centimeters, and millions of smaller fragments that can still damage spacecraft because they travel at about 28,000 kilometers per hour. A single collision can create thousands of new fragments, which can cause further collisions, a chain reaction known as the Kessler syndrome. To reduce the danger, regulators now require satellites in low orbit to be removed within five years of the end of their missions, and companies are developing technologies to capture and remove defunct satellites. Experts say that stronger international coordination is needed.
target_summary: Growing satellite numbers raise collision and debris risks.

source: Bamboo is a grass that grows up to one meter a day, and it reaches maturity in three to five years, whereas many trees take 30 years or more. Its fibers are strong in tension, comparable to some steels, which makes it useful for scaffolding, flooring, and building frames. Engineered bamboo products, made by laminating strips with adhesive, are increasingly used for beams and panels. A two-story community school built in Vietnam with a frame of treated bamboo cost about 40 percent less than a similar concrete building. The material has drawbacks: untreated bamboo is vulnerable to insects and rot, and building codes in many countries do not yet cover it, which makes approval difficult. Researchers are working on treatments that extend its life to 50 years and on standards.
target_summary: Bamboo grows fast and is strong but needs treatment and standards.

source: The Kibale Ridge Eco-Lodge, which opened in 2019 on the edge of a rainforest reserve in Uganda, employs 62 people from nearby villages and runs entirely on solar power. Its 12 guest cabins are built from local timber and stone, rainwater is collected for showers, and waste water is filtered through a reed bed. Guests pay 240 dollars per night, and 10 percent of revenue is paid into a fund that has built a clinic and two classrooms. Visitors can take guided walks to see chimpanzees, but groups are limited to six people. The lodge says that occupancy averaged 71 percent last year. Critics point out that many guests arrive by long-haul flights, which produce far more carbon emissions than the lodge saves, and the owners are looking at offsetting these emissions through tree planting.
target_summary: Kibale Ridge Eco-Lodge runs on solar power and funds community projects.

source: People who spend long hours at computers often experience digital eye strain, which includes dry eyes, headaches, blurred vision, and sore neck muscles. A major cause is that people blink about half as often when looking at a screen, so the surface of the eye dries out. Eye specialists recommend the 20-20-20 rule: every 20 minutes, look at something at least 20 feet, about six meters, away for 20 seconds. Other measures include placing the screen about an arm's length away with the top slightly below eye level, reducing glare from windows and lamps, and using artificial tears if the eyes feel dry. Contrary to popular belief, screens do not cause permanent damage to eyesight, and blue-light glasses have not been shown to reduce symptoms in controlled trials.
target_summary: The 20-20-20 rule helps prevent digital eye strain.

source: The Great Fire of Alderton began on the night of 14 September 1743 in a bakery on Cooper Lane and burned for four days, destroying 1,100 buildings, about two thirds of the walled town. Winds fanned the flames through narrow streets lined with timber houses and thatched roofs, and the town's three hand-pumped fire engines were unable to reach the area. About 40 people died, and an estimated 6,000 were left homeless. Afterward, the town council banned thatch and required new buildings to be made of brick or stone, and it widened main streets to at least 12 meters so that they would act as firebreaks. The rebuilding took 17 years and was financed partly by donations from other towns and a tax on coal. The pattern of wide streets can still be seen in the town center.
target_summary: The 1743 Great Fire of Alderton destroyed two thirds of the town.

source: A fixed-rate mortgage keeps the same interest rate for a set period, usually 15 or 30 years, so monthly payments do not change, while a variable-rate mortgage has an interest rate that moves with market rates. Variable loans often start with a lower rate, which can save money if rates stay low or fall, but borrowers face the risk of higher payments when rates rise. For example, on a 250,000 dollar loan over 25 years, a rise of two percentage points in the interest rate can add about 300 dollars to the monthly payment. Fixed loans give certainty and protect against rate increases, but borrowers may pay more if rates fall, and they usually face penalties for leaving the loan early. Financial advisers say that the right choice depends on how much uncertainty a household can tolerate.
target_summary: Fixed mortgages give stable payments; variable ones start cheaper but risk increases.

source: Smart thermostats, which learn a household's routine and adjust heating and cooling automatically, can reduce energy use, but the savings are smaller than advertised. A study of 5,000 homes found that devices saved an average of 8 percent on heating and 10 percent on cooling, equal to about 130 dollars per year, compared with manufacturers' claims of 20 to 30 percent. Savings were greatest in homes where residents previously kept the temperature constant all day, and smallest in those that already used manual setbacks. The devices cost from 120 to 250 dollars, so payback typically takes one to two years. Experts advise choosing a model that works with the home's heating system, setting a schedule that lowers the temperature when nobody is home, and checking that the temperature sensor is not near a window or heat source.
target_summary: Smart thermostats save less energy than advertised, about 130 dollars yearly.

source: Urban coyotes have settled in cities across North America, with an estimated 2,000 living in the Greater Marlow area alone. They feed on rodents, rabbits, fruit, and food waste, and most avoid people. Reports of coyote attacks on pets, however, have increased by 35 percent in three years, prompting some residents to demand culling. Wildlife biologists say that killing coyotes is ineffective because other coyotes move into the vacant territory and often breed more, so the population recovers within a year. Instead, the city runs a coexistence program that teaches residents to secure garbage, avoid feeding wildlife, keep small pets indoors at dawn and dusk, and scare coyotes away by shouting and waving their arms. Since the program began, reported conflicts in participating neighborhoods have fallen by 28 percent.
target_summary: Coexistence education reduced urban coyote conflicts 28 percent.

source: The city of Lakewood has approved a new licensing system for street food vendors that allows 400 permits, compared with a cap of 150 that has been in place since 1989. Under the old system, many vendors operated without permits and risked fines of up to 500 dollars and confiscation of their equipment. The new permits cost 180 dollars per year, require a food safety course, and allow vendors to operate in designated zones near transit stations and parks. Supporters say that street food provides affordable meals, jobs for immigrants and people without formal qualifications, and lively public spaces. Some restaurant owners are concerned about competition and trash, and the city will require vendors to clean the area within five meters of their carts. A review is planned after 18 months.
target_summary: Lakewood will license 400 street food vendors instead of 150.

source: A 15 billion dollar semiconductor factory under construction in the Arizona desert will start producing advanced chips in 2027 and employ about 3,000 people. The plant, built by Atlas Microelectronics, will use roughly 17 million liters of water per day, which it plans to recycle at a rate of 85 percent, and it will be powered partly by a nearby solar farm. Chip production is highly complex and requires clean rooms that are thousands of times cleaner than a hospital operating room, since a single dust particle can ruin a chip. The project is supported by 2.1 billion dollars in government subsidies, aimed at reducing dependence on factories in East Asia, where most advanced chips are made. Local colleges have begun training programs for technicians, but the company says that finding enough skilled workers is a major challenge.
target_summary: Atlas Microelectronics is building a 15 billion dollar Arizona chip factory.

source: Fifty years ago, the Tamsin River, which runs through the industrial city of Brantwick, was so polluted that fish could not survive in it, and a 1969 report described its water as the color of rust. A cleanup effort that began in 1975 required factories to treat their waste water and led to the construction of three sewage treatment plants, funded by a levy on water bills. Dissolved oxygen levels have risen from near zero to healthy levels, and last year biologists counted 38 species of fish, including salmon, which returned for the first time in 90 years. The riverbank has been transformed into a 14-kilometer park with trails and kayak launches. Problems remain, however: heavy rain still causes sewers to overflow, releasing untreated waste into the river about eight times a year, and a 600 million dollar tunnel project aims to fix this by 2030.
target_summary: The Tamsin River recovered from severe pollution, now hosting 38 fish species.
